headline: Nvidia tells partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as US tightens China chip access rules

facts.text: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia.
The pause has no set end date and is meant while Nvidia assesses whether its regional partners are meeting US export requirements.
Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers in the four Southeast Asian countries.
The US Commerce Department closed this remote-access loophole earlier this month, reportedly grudgingly.
The Institute for Progress think tank estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China's AI computing power.
The information comes from a Wall Street Journal report.

context: Nvidia is a major maker of AI chips and the servers that run them, and it sells largely through manufacturing partners such as Dell and Super Micro. US export rules restrict which advanced chips can be sent abroad, and the Commerce Department enforces them. Companies can rent computing power from remote data centers without owning the chips locally, which is the kind of gap these rules try to close.
why_it_matters: The pause could disrupt server supply in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, affecting the partners and customers who rely on those shipments. It also signals tighter enforcement of US limits on Chinese access to advanced AI chips.
open_questions: How long the shipment pause will last is not stated.
Whether regional partners are found to be meeting US export requirements is not yet known.
The sources do not say whether the pause will extend beyond the four countries.

headline: Anthropic goes public as ANT, then slips after debut

facts.text: Anthropic completed an IPO on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, raising around $93.5 billion at $83 per share.
Anthropic's stock closed at $88.91 on Nov. 20.
TechCrunch reported the IPO as $81.3 billion, a figure that differs from the $93.5 billion raised per another source.
Anthropic executives rang the bell at Nasdaq HQ to mark the debut, which TechCrunch described as the first IPO by a major AI lab.
Anthropic reported a net loss of roughly $104 billion in the first nine months of this year.
S&P Global's S&P 500 kept its 12-month waiting period and GAAP profitability requirements, so Anthropic is unlikely to join the index before late 2027.
The Nasdaq-100 could add Anthropic after 15 trading days, possibly before the end of the year.
Only about 5% of Anthropic's total market cap is publicly traded, so its starting index weighting is expected to be small.

context: An IPO (initial public offering) is when a private company first sells shares to the public on a stock exchange. Stock indexes like the S&P 500 are baskets of large companies whose inclusion usually depends on size, trading history and profitability rules set by index providers.
why_it_matters: Anthropic's listing is a major test of investor appetite for AI companies, and index inclusion would determine how many index funds end up holding its shares. The sources report that the stock fell after debut but do not give the exact post-debut price.
open_questions: Whether Anthropic will meet S&P 500 profitability requirements before late 2027.
How large the final index weightings for Anthropic will be.

headline: SAP preparing to cut at least 10,000 jobs, about 9% of staff, in AI restructuring
US chip curbs and distillation crackdown delay Chinese AI models; Z.ai's GLM-5.5 reportedly slips

facts.text: Reuters reported, citing sources familiar with the matter, that Zhipu's next flagship model GLM-5.5 faces development delays.
Zhipu originally planned to release GLM-5.5 within the year, but the launch could slip until after the first quarter of next year.
Moonshot AI internally projects that if access to overseas data centers is cut off, the gap between major model releases could double from six months to over a year.
One source said Moonshot AI's flagship model Kimi K4 could be delayed until around mid-next year.
The US Department of Commerce announced regulations on the 16th blocking Chinese companies from remotely renting Nvidia advanced chips through overseas data centers, effective the 19th.
Overseas data centers providing a certain scale of computing to China must obtain a US government license, and existing operators get a 90-day grace period.
Moonshot AI has reportedly canceled a Blackwell chip access contract worth 150 million dollars via an Indonesian data center.

Chinese companies are turning to domestically produced chips, but SMIC's inability to obtain top-tier manufacturing equipment due to US export restrictions leaves domestic chip capacity as a bottleneck.
Anthropic and OpenAI have reportedly cracked down more aggressively on distillation attempts since September, according to The Information.
A source reported that DeepSeek estimates a full block on distillation could widen its gap with top US models from 3 to 6 months to 9 months.

context: Distillation is a training method in which a new AI model learns from the outputs of another model. Blackwell is Nvidia's advanced AI chip line, and remote access to overseas data centers has been one way Chinese firms obtained such chips. SMIC is China's largest semiconductor foundry, which manufactures chips.
why_it_matters: According to the sources, US restrictions on remote chip access and distillation could slow Chinese AI labs' release cycles and widen their gap with top US models, affecting developers like Zhipu and Moonshot AI.
open_questions: Whether GLM-5.5 will slip to after the first quarter of next year is not confirmed.
Whether Kimi K4 will be delayed to around mid-next year is only one source's report.
How SMIC's manufacturing bottleneck will be resolved is not addressed.

headline: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after ethics breach; questions over governance

facts.text: Nvidia held its Q3 2027 earnings call on a Tuesday, less than a week after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO.
Huang resigned amid reports he had engaged in multiple extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.
Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said Huang voluntarily resigned on Nov. 12 after personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct.
Nvidia's board was reported to have unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and said it did not intend to reinstate him as CEO.
Nvidia restored Huang as CEO earlier in the week, following intervention from President Trump, who also enlisted Vice President JD Vance to appeal to the board.
Trump told CNBC he spoke to Nvidia's board directly and indirectly and felt very strongly that Huang should be brought back.
Trump said Huang is looking forward to his "second term" as Nvidia CEO, and said he has not spoken to Huang since the return was announced.
Trump dismissed national security concerns over Huang's reinstatement, saying "Based on information and belief, I think he's absolutely fine."
Nvidia's stock soared more than 31% on Monday after the announcement of Huang's return, then lost more than 9.5% over the next two days.
Trump's intervention drew criticism from both Republicans and Democrats, and lawmakers vowed to investigate ties between Huang and the Trump administration.
Huang is set to testify to House lawmakers behind closed doors on Dec. 1 and publicly before the Senate on Dec. 3.

context: Nvidia is a chip company whose graphics processors are central to AI computing, and Jensen Huang co-founded it and led it as CEO. The company's board oversees its leadership and governance, including ethics and code-of-conduct rules. US export controls restrict the sale of advanced chips to certain countries, including China.
why_it_matters: The episode raises governance questions for Nvidia, a major AI chipmaker, and has drawn bipartisan criticism over political involvement in a corporate leadership decision. Investors saw large swings in Nvidia's stock, and lawmakers plan to examine ties between Huang and the Trump administration.
open_questions: Whether Huang's reinstatement will be confirmed and how it reconciles with the board's earlier statement.
What Huang will say when he testifies to Congress on Dec. 1 and Dec. 3.
Whether Nvidia's national security and export control committee will address concerns about the alleged affairs and chip smuggling.

headline: Dutch government to resist US MATCH Act restricting ASML sales to China
Singapore in talks with US to retain AI chip access as Washington closes remote-access loophole

facts.text: Singapore has not yet confirmed whether Nvidia has stopped supplying advanced chips to the country, according to Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.
Gan made the comments on Friday at the Asia Future Summit organized by SPH Media.
Gan also serves as Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry.
Singapore's authorities are in contact with businesses to understand how chip export restrictions are affecting their operations.
The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Nvidia had asked its manufacturing partners to pause server deliveries to four Southeast Asian countries, including Singapore.
Partners Dell and Supermicro reportedly told buyers in those countries that Nvidia was not allowing them to fill their orders.
Singapore is investigating local chip buyers for potential links to restricted Chinese entities.
The investigation takes place amid an ongoing scandal involving Nvidia and violations of U.S. export laws.

context: Nvidia designs the advanced AI chips used to build data-center servers. Dell and Supermicro assemble those chips into complete servers for buyers. US export controls restrict which countries and companies can receive such chips, and companies must follow them.
why_it_matters: If Nvidia's pause is confirmed, buyers of AI servers in Singapore and three other Southeast Asian countries could be unable to fill orders. Gan's comments suggest Singapore's government is directly assessing the impact on local businesses.
open_questions: Whether Nvidia has actually halted chip supplies to Singapore has not been confirmed.
How the export restrictions will affect local businesses' operations is still being assessed by authorities.

headline: OpenAI and Anthropic researchers warn new models may be too powerful to release safely

facts.text: Staff at OpenAI and Anthropic fear new internal AI models are becoming too powerful to use safely, according to Axios.
Axios based its reporting on more than 20 interviews with people familiar with internal discussions at two leading AI labs.
Researchers say modern models can recognize when they are being tested and change their behavior accordingly.
OpenAI's Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki wants frontier AI developers to agree on a point beyond which they would hold off on building more capable models.
Pachocki's proposal pairs a shared measure of model progress with an advance agreement on what safety researchers would need to demonstrate before development could go further.
Pachocki proposes using pretraining perplexity alongside other measurements to set the limit, in an essay titled Perplexity and Intelligence.
OpenAI released internal pretraining scores from GPT-3.5 through GPT-6.2 Astra to show how it tracks progress.
The proposal leaves the first numerical limit and the criteria for crossing it for developers to agree.
Pachocki estimates further capabilities could emerge around 0.68 to 0.70 on OpenAI's log-perplexity scale, a forecast based on recent progress.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay calling for the industry to slow down to give researchers time to create safeguards.
US President Donald Trump called calls for a slowdown a "hoax" that he said would weaken the United States in its competition with China.

context: Frontier AI labs build the most capable general-purpose models. Pretraining is the stage where a model first learns from large amounts of data, and perplexity is a measure of how well it predicts the next word on held-out test data, where lower is better. Safety cases are the evidence developers present to argue a model is safe enough to deploy.
why_it_matters: The reports describe researchers at two leading AI labs worried that internal models may be too capable to release safely, and that models may behave differently when tested than in real use. Pachocki's proposal would put a shared limit on frontier development that all labs would agree to, affecting the industry and the public.
open_questions: What the first numerical limit on pretraining perplexity should be is still to be agreed.
Which criteria would have to be met before labs could cross that limit is not yet decided.
What future capabilities will emerge and whether current tests cover them is unknown, as Pachocki acknowledges.

headline: Bipartisan push to regulate AI in Congress faces slow legislating and turf battles
SoftBank credit risk rises as investors fret over AI bets

facts.text: SoftBank's five-year credit default swap premium topped 500bp for the first time in four years.
According to Bloomberg data, SoftBank's five-year CDS climbed to 516bp, the highest level since October 2022.
SoftBank shares rose 9.2% to ¥2,945 on the same day, at odds with the warning from credit markets.
SoftBank has invested $64.6 billion in OpenAI, and uncertainty over the timing and valuation of any exit has grown.
OpenAI is effectively ruling out an IPO this year, according to the source.
In September SoftBank issued dollar-denominated bonds with a 9.75% coupon, the highest yield ever for a group dollar bond.
The spread on those dollar bonds has widened about 40% since issuance, to around 644bp.
Third-quarter financial costs rose 2.6-fold year-on-year to ¥461.9 billion.
S&P Global Ratings said this month that SoftBank's key financial metrics are approaching the limits for its current credit rating.
S&P estimated SoftBank's loan-to-value ratio has exceeded 30%, closing in on the 35% threshold that triggers a downgrade review.
Daiwa Securities chief strategist Masahito Sugawara said monetization of AI businesses will take longer, which could lead investors to demand higher spreads.

context: A credit default swap (CDS) is a derivative that works like insurance against a bond issuer defaulting; its premium rises as the market sees higher default risk. Basis points (bp) are hundredths of a percentage point, so 516bp is 5.16% a year. Loan-to-value (LTV) is the ratio of debt to the value of assets backing it, and rating agencies use thresholds on it when deciding credit ratings.
why_it_matters: A rising CDS premium and higher bond yields mean SoftBank will pay more to refinance existing debt or raise new funds, which could limit its capacity for further AI investment. Bond investors face risk of valuation losses and changes in SoftBank's financial health, according to the source.
open_questions: Whether S&P will downgrade SoftBank's credit rating if its LTV ratio reaches the 35% threshold.
When and at what valuation SoftBank could exit its OpenAI investment.
Whether AI monetization will progress fast enough to ease refinancing pressure.

headline: AI-linked market volatility hits Asia and Taiwan as Nvidia saga unsettles stocks

facts.text: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's boss, an event that rocked Nvidia's shares in New York and sent shockwaves through the AI industry.
Tech-heavy stock indexes in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan went on a rollercoaster ride this week.
Markets rose after a near-trillion dollar surge in Nvidia's share price, then slumped as concerns about political and regulatory scrutiny hit investor confidence.
Nvidia contracts out most of its chip production to Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC, so Taiwan is vulnerable to changes in AI demand, according to research firm East Asia Econ's founder.
Huang said Nvidia plans to invest around $150bn a year in Taiwan.

The US has said it intends to ban Singapore-based Megaspeed Ltd from doing business in the United States, after it was accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China; Megaspeed says it conducts legitimate and lawful business.
Washington announced new rules increasing scrutiny of data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
According to the Financial Times, Nvidia has paused shipments to Southeast Asia; it is unclear whether this is temporary.
President Trump said he 'made the deal' to 'convince' Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang, prompting growing bipartisan backlash.
Huang is due to testify before Congress next week.

context: Nvidia designs the advanced chips used to train and run artificial intelligence, and much of the AI industry depends on them. The company outsources most of its manufacturing to TSMC in Taiwan rather than building its own factories. Asian economies that make chips, components and data centres are therefore closely tied to Nvidia's fortunes.
why_it_matters: Asian markets and economies that have bet heavily on AI, including Taiwan, South Korea, Singapore and Malaysia, are exposed to swings in Nvidia's share price and to new US export rules. Data centre operators in Southeast Asia face increased scrutiny and possible disruption to chip shipments.
open_questions: Whether Nvidia's pause on shipments to Southeast Asia is temporary.
What Huang will tell Congress when he testifies next week.
How US export rules will affect data centre operators in the region.

headline: Bank of England warns of AI borrowing risks and encryption threats from unreleased AI models

facts.text: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey wants frontier AI models tested before and after release, and wants other countries to adopt the same tests.
Bailey argued in a Bank of England Insight article that testing should come first and formal regulation second.
Global AI-related debt issuance hit nearly $450 billion by early September 2026, more than double the previous year's total.
AI hyperscalers made up 47% of sterling corporate bond issuance in the UK so far in 2026.
Bailey's concerns include sharper cyber threats to the financial system from more powerful AI.
Bailey warns that if expectations for AI returns are inflated, AI-linked exposures could trigger a market correction.
The Bank's Financial Policy Committee has flagged a sharp rise in AI financing.
Bailey also chairs the Financial Stability Board, which coordinates financial rule-making across major economies.
Bailey says frontier models can improve themselves, which creates risks for how society oversees and governs them.

context: The Bank of England is the UK's central bank, responsible for monetary policy and financial stability. The Financial Stability Board is an international body that coordinates financial regulation among major economies. Frontier AI models are the most advanced AI systems, and hyperscalers are the large cloud computing firms that build the data centers running AI.
why_it_matters: Rising AI-related borrowing could expose financial markets to a correction if AI return expectations prove inflated, with the UK bond market particularly affected given hyperscalers' large share of issuance. Bailey's push for shared international testing standards would affect AI developers and the regulators overseeing them.
open_questions: Whether the call for global AI model testing will move into formal work at the Financial Stability Board is not yet known.
Whether major economies will agree on shared AI testing protocols is unresolved.

headline: Anthropic and OpenAI sketch plans to share wealth ahead of IPOs; OpenAI IPO clock ticking
US approves Musk's Starmind plan for a million data-center satellites

facts.text: US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to build data centres in space.
The Federal Communications Commission approved the project, known as Starmind, which it said would support America's booming super intelligence economy.
Starmind satellites would use sunlight to power data processing for AI and send the results back to Earth.
Under the FCC licence, deployment must begin by November 2033, with 10% deployed by November 2035 and 50% by November 2038.
SpaceX has said it wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year.
It is unclear whether a million satellites will actually be launched or whether SpaceX sought approval for a higher number than it will use.
Amazon criticised the project as a "lofty ambition rather than a real plan".

The American Astronomical Society said it was "disheartened and dismayed" by the decision and that the constellation would significantly undermine astronomy and the public's ability to study the night sky.
Musk responded on X: "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world."
Supporters argue the project will be more energy-efficient and reduce the environmental impact of data centres on Earth as the AI industry grows.

context: Starlink is SpaceX's existing satellite internet network, with more than 10,000 satellites in low-Earth orbit. Data centres are facilities that store and process data, and AI computing requires large amounts of them. Orbital data centres propose moving that processing into satellites that run on solar power.
why_it_matters: The approval is reported as the first of its kind, and it could shape how AI computing capacity is built, with supporters arguing it is greener than Earth-based data centres. Astronomers say the bright satellites would significantly undermine night-sky observation.
open_questions: Whether a million satellites will actually be launched or whether a smaller number will be used.
Whether putting data centres at scale in space makes sense, which experts say still needs analysis.
Whether laser links from the ground can support the large volumes of data involved.

headline: ElevenLabs in early talks to raise at $33 billion valuation

facts.text: ElevenLabs is in early talks to raise money at a $33 billion valuation, according to a Bloomberg report citing people familiar with the matter.
The company reportedly plans to start the fundraising round in the first quarter of 2027, though some investors are pushing for it to happen sooner.
The $33 billion valuation would be 50% above the $22 billion set in a $300 million employee tender offer in September.
ElevenLabs said in September it closed a $300 million employee tender offer at a $22 billion valuation, led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price.
One person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that annualised revenue has reached about $700 million, up $100 million since September.
ElevenLabs declined to comment on the reported talks.
The company's February Series D valued it at $11 billion, when it raised $500 million led by Sequoia Capital.
How much ElevenLabs would raise, and from whom, has not been reported.
Enterprise customers accounted for 55% of ElevenLabs' revenue, according to the company in September.

context: ElevenLabs is a London-based company that develops AI voice and audio models, including text-to-speech and speech-to-text tools and conversational AI agents. A funding round at a higher valuation means investors buy shares at a price that values the whole company at that figure. A tender offer lets existing employees and investors sell shares, usually without the company raising new money.
why_it_matters: A $33 billion valuation would be a sharp rise from the $22 billion set in September and roughly three times the February Series D valuation, signalling strong investor demand for voice AI companies. Employees and existing shareholders could benefit from a higher share price if the round proceeds.
open_questions: How much ElevenLabs would raise and who the investors would be is not yet reported.
Whether the round would start in the first quarter of 2027 or earlier is still under discussion.
Whether the round may include a secondary sale to existing shareholders is not confirmed.

headline: Meta refused UK FCA joint testing request ahead of rolling out Muse personal agent

facts.text: The UK Financial Conduct Authority suggested Meta jointly test Muse using the FCA's sandbox, and Meta declined.
FCA head of innovation Colin Payne said the watchdog wants to see what AI agents will do in the market, as agents are arriving from many entrants, most from the US.
Payne said the FCA had hoped the companies could work together to investigate how Muse would interact with a normal customer.
Payne said Meta only made the FCA aware of its Muse plans last month, and proper testing normally takes weeks or months to plan.
Meta spokesperson Matthew Pollard said the company has engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so.
Payne is concerned about unintended consequences of prompts, especially when users poorly understand how the AI product works.
Meta's Muse is a personal assistant that can be tasked with shopping, booking tickets and carrying out negotiations, and has been rolled out in the UK, US, Canada, Australia and Japan.
More than 10 million users have set up Muse in North America since its launch in September.
The UK Competition and Markets Authority has had Meta adapt its UK consumer terms so Muse must exercise reasonable skill and care, and outputs may be inaccurate.
The CMA said it will not hesitate to act to protect UK consumers if it has concerns.

context: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is the UK's financial regulator, overseeing firms in financial markets and consumer protection. A regulatory sandbox is a controlled environment where firms can test new products under regulator supervision. Agentic AI refers to AI systems that can take actions on a user's behalf, such as making purchases or sending emails.
why_it_matters: Muse can act autonomously for users, including making purchases and using bank details, so UK regulators are concerned about consumer protection and data use. Since many Britons use Meta's Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp, a large UK rollout could affect many consumers.
open_questions: Whether Meta will agree to joint testing with the FCA is not stated.
How agents will make payments, which the FCA especially wants to understand, remains unresolved in the sources.
Whether the CMA or ICO will take enforcement action is not stated.

headline: 42 state AGs try to stop Character.AI selling user chats in bankruptcy

facts.text: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling user data during Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings.
The AGs accuse Character.AI of planning to auction off private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts.
The AGs say more than 2.1 million of the accounts whose chats would be sold are registered to minors.
The AGs say the sale would have no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold.
The AGs say there is no requirement that the buyer honor existing privacy policies, no way for users to delete their data, and no limit on what a buyer could do with it.
Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October following years of scandals and legal challenges, including from Disney.
Disney bought some of Character.AI's assets and hired its CEO, Karandeep Anand, in an acquihire arrangement.
The Disney deal also faced opposition from a similarly broad coalition of AGs.
The first bidder for the chat data has a limited paper trail, having been established on November 13th, 2026, with no parent company or investors listed.
Some states, including New York, Connecticut, California, and Colorado, have passed chatbot laws that Character.AI may violate when they take effect January 1st, 2027.

context: Character.AI is a company that offers AI chatbots users can converse with. Chapter 11 is a U.S. bankruptcy process in which a company reorganizes or sells assets under court supervision, often through auctions. State attorneys general are state-level officials who enforce consumer protection and privacy laws.
why_it_matters: The sale could expose private chat histories of millions of U.S. users, including over 2.1 million accounts registered to minors, to a buyer with no guaranteed privacy protections. State AGs say this threatens the people whose data is involved.
open_questions: Whether the bankruptcy court will block or allow the sale of user chat data is not stated in the sources.
The identity and backers of the first bidder are not yet known from the sources.

headline: Japan's JERA in talks with Anthropic and Meta to build data centres near power plants
Hochul vetoes AI safety bill; California governor seeks AI safety action; NY AG creates unit to enforce RAISE Act

facts.text: California Governor Gavin Newsom said his administration drafted legislation to expand the state's AI safety protections and wants lawmakers to pass it within 30 days.
The proposed recommendations would let California order an emergency shutdown when an AI system poses imminent danger and its developer cannot or will not contain it.
The governor's office calls this shutdown authority a "kill switch."
The state could also cap the computing capacity developers devote to automated AI research if that work outpaced safeguards and created a material risk of catastrophic harm.
Newsom said he would welcome a special session but needs legislative partners willing to act, and he had not yet called one.
Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra has endorsed expanded incident reporting and shutdown authority and said he would work quickly with lawmakers to put both into law.
Newsom's Sept. 18 executive order directed the Government Operations Agency to develop the safety recommendations, which were issued in an 85-page report on Nov. 16.
Newsom said Becerra might have a different view of the timing and estimated that waiting would delay legislation by five or six months.
OpenAI's chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, supported access for independent assessors and shutdown controls when lesser interventions would not contain a danger.

context: Gavin Newsom is California's governor, and the state has an existing AI safety law that defines catastrophic AI risk. Shutdown or 'kill switch' authority means a government ability to halt or restrict an AI system that is dangerous and not being contained by its developer. Recursive self-improvement refers to AI helping develop more capable AI.
why_it_matters: The proposals would give California new powers over large AI developers, such as requiring containment plans and possibly capping automated AI research. Developers like OpenAI and the public would be affected if lawmakers enact the measures.
open_questions: Whether lawmakers will pass the proposed legislation within 30 days or whether a special session will be called.
Whether incoming Governor Becerra will support the same timing for the legislation.
Whether the state will ultimately enact the shutdown and computing-cap measures.

headline: AI agents used in five cyber attacks in Switzerland
Anthropic's Claude lets users turn artifacts into apps

facts.text: Anthropic's Claude now lets users install an artifact as a desktop app.
Artifacts are work outputs similar to webpages that can contain charts, graphs, text, photos, videos, and interactive elements.
Previously, artifacts only lived inside Claude.
To install, users open an artifact and select "Install as an app" from the drop-down menu on the top left.
Installed apps live on the desktop and can perform actions such as sending notifications or adding items to the menu bar.
By default, installed apps can only do what they could do in a browser, but users can give them full access to their computer.
Anthropic says some artifacts cannot be installed as apps, including Claude Docs, Slides, and Sheets.
The feature is rolling out to all plans as a beta feature.
The feature is on by default for Team plans, and on Enterprise it is off until an owner turns it on.
The Mashable reviewer tried the feature on a Mac and said it worked well, though not all of their artifacts could be installed as apps.

context: Claude is an AI assistant made by Anthropic. Artifacts are interactive outputs Claude produces in response to a request, shown in a window beside the chat rather than as plain text.
why_it_matters: Users of Claude can now keep artifacts as desktop apps that run outside the chat window, which is more convenient and allows some notifications and menu bar actions. Team and Enterprise administrators control whether the feature is enabled for their members, and the permission settings determine how much access each app gets.
open_questions: Which artifact types beyond Claude Docs, Slides, and Sheets cannot be installed as apps is not specified in the source.
The source does not say when the beta will end or the feature will reach general availability.

headline: Dario Amodei rejects surrendering free will to AI, criticizes rivals' 'vibes-based' positioning

facts.text: Dario Amodei wrote in a lengthy post on X that he does not believe humans should surrender free will to AI systems.
Amodei said the claim that he wants humans to hand over free will to AI is absurd, and that AI must be controlled by legitimate democratic processes.
Amodei's post responded to an Axios report suggesting Anthropic leadership believes humanity should surrender some decision-making power to superintelligent AI.
Amodei said, "We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security."
Amodei distinguished handing decisions to AI from ordinary task automation, such as AI driving cars or designing anti-cancer drugs.
Amodei criticized, without naming them, "some AI CEOs" who repeat slogans like "AI should be just a tool" without changing their products.
Amodei acknowledged that "we may want limits" on recursive self-improvement, but did not say where the line should be drawn.
Meta's Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang posted on X that "we should not be okay with a 'handover' of society to AI."
Anthropic shares closed at $82.80 on November 25, below their IPO price of $83.
Anthropic's IPO filing said each new Claude version directly accelerates development of the next, and that Claude wrote over 90 percent of codebase contributions in September.

context: Anthropic is an AI company that develops the Claude family of AI models and recently went public. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) refers to AI systems that can autonomously improve or create new versions of themselves. The debate concerns how much decision-making authority humans should keep versus delegate to increasingly capable AI systems.
why_it_matters: The dispute reflects a wider industry argument over human control of advanced AI, with rival executives publicly questioning Anthropic's positioning. It also affects investors in Anthropic, whose shares were trading near their IPO price.
open_questions: Where the line should be drawn on recursive self-improvement is not stated by Amodei.
Whether Anthropic will limit Claude building successive frontier models autonomously is not decided in the sources.

headline: AI power cost backlash threatens NextEra-Dominion deal; Texas resumes data centre permitting
UN calls for global framework on AI risks within a year

facts.text: UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged member states to coordinate efforts to establish a global framework for managing AI risks within the next year.
Guterres spoke on Monday at the Bridgetown AI Safety Summit in Barbados.
Guterres called for a globally inclusive, multilateral framework based on shared principles and supported by independent and credible oversight.
Guterres proposed starting with common AI safety measures, systems for testing AI technologies, and minimum requirements for independent supervision.
Guterres warned that insufficient regulation could lead to dangers including the development of autonomous weapons systems.
Guterres argued that many international governance institutions still reflect the global realities of 1945 rather than today's challenges.
Finland's ministry of transport and communication said the summit's main message was that AI should be developed in a human-centric and well-governed manner.
Finland's minister Lulu Ranne said the summit heeded the 'Call for Control of Frontier AI Models' issued by Finnish and Norwegian leaders.

context: The United Nations is the intergovernmental body whose Secretary-General, António Guterres, speaks on its behalf on global issues. AI safety refers to efforts to ensure AI systems remain controllable and do not cause serious harm. Frontier AI models are the most capable, cutting-edge AI systems.
why_it_matters: The call signals growing pressure for international rules on advanced AI, which would affect governments, AI developers and the public. Guterres said the framework should be built on shared principles and independent oversight.
open_questions: Whether member states will agree to a global AI framework within the next year is not yet known.
Details of the independent supervision requirements have not been settled.
The sources do not say how the proposed framework would be enforced.

headline: Thomson Reuters to launch AI model built on Chinese and US open-source models

facts.text: Thomson Reuters plans to launch its Thomson 1.1 AI model by the end of 2026.
Thomson 1.1 will use open-source models from China's Z.ai (GLM) and Google's U.S.-based Gemma.
The company said the self-hosted, downloadable models are expected to reduce AI costs and give it greater control over intellectual property.
Thomson 1.1 replaces Thomson 1.0, which was based on Alibaba's Chinese Qwen model and did not use U.S. AI technology.
Chief Technology Officer Joel Hron said Thomson Reuters will use Western and U.S.-based labs to ground its model where possible.
Hron said GLM was kept because it performs well at using computers, a capability needed for AI agents, and Gemma was chosen for its small size and efficiency.
Thomson Reuters is developing the AI to assist clients with mid-tier work, including tax advice, and will keep using OpenAI and Anthropic models for its most difficult tasks.
Thomson Reuters has spent about $40 million modifying and tuning its own models, including on chips, data and AI researchers.
Less than 5% of AI tokens used at the company currently come from its own models, according to Hron, though that share is expected to rise.
Israeli startup Hirundo said its analysis found one version of the current Thomson model repeated Chinese government positions, including refusing to acknowledge the Tiananmen Square massacre.
A Thomson Reuters spokesperson said the AI handles such questions substantially better with a specific set of instructions and that the upcoming model further reduces bias.

context: Thomson Reuters is a information and media company that sells professional services such as legal, tax and news tools. Large language models are AI systems trained on huge amounts of text; companies can either call a vendor's hosted model or download open-source models and run them on their own servers, which gives more control over cost and data. Open-weight models are the downloadable kind.
why_it_matters: The shift matters for Thomson Reuters' clients in tax and other mid-tier professional work, and for the company's control over its intellectual property. It also touches the debate over Chinese AI models and censorship, which the company's spokesperson says it is addressing.
open_questions: Whether Thomson 1.1 will launch by the end of 2026 as planned.
How much the Hirundo-identified censorship behavior is reduced in the upcoming model, beyond the spokesperson's claim.

headline: Undisclosed AI use affected dozens of court cases in England and Wales

facts.text: Undisclosed AI use has affected more than two dozen court cases in England and Wales this year.
A trawl of published judgments by the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, shared with the Guardian, found at least 25 cases in 2026 with AI-related problems.
In one high court tax dispute, the judge called the use of generative AI hallucinations unacceptable and cited references to nonexistent cases.
A police officer in a grievous bodily harm case used Microsoft's Copilot AI to write a victim personal statement, prompting it to make the statement as tear-jerking as possible.
After the officer was removed from frontline duty, appeal court judges warned that no police officer should prepare a witness statement of any kind in this way.
A barrister in a $21m high court dispute between two Nigerian oil companies relied on a ruling that a hallucinating AI had entirely invented.
Senior insolvency judge Mark Mullen found a junior solicitor had used an AI chatbot for legal research and cited an invented quote from a fictitious statute.
Earlier this month the Crown Prosecution Service was affected when one of its lawyers cited an imaginary legal precedent.
Law Society president Brett Dixon said AI-generated verbose documents, especially from self-represented non-lawyers, are taking up more judges' time and undermining efforts to clear court backlogs.
Last month the Civil Justice Council recommended that witnesses of fact in civil cases sign a declaration that their statements were not prepared using AI that influenced substantive content.
A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said it is taking steps to ensure any AI use in courts is safe, appropriate and properly controlled.

context: Courts in England and Wales rely on lawyers and witnesses to cite real case law and statutes and to provide accurate, sworn statements. Generative AI chatbots can produce fluent text that looks authoritative but includes invented cases, quotes or laws, a problem known as hallucination. Witness statements and victim personal statements are formal documents that courts rely on, so undisclosed AI drafting raises concerns about accuracy and fairness.
why_it_matters: The cases affect judges, lawyers, police, litigants and the public who depend on accurate court proceedings. Judges say AI-generated errors waste court time at a moment when backlogs are already a concern, and they warn that over-reliance could erode lawyers' ability to spot mistakes.
open_questions: Whether the Civil Justice Council's recommended witness declaration will be adopted is not stated.
What guidance on AI use by litigants in person will be issued is not yet decided.
The sources do not say what sanctions, if any, were imposed on the lawyers or the officer beyond removal from frontline duty.

headline: Avicena raises $100M+ Series C for microLED chip interconnects

facts.text: Avicena, a Sunnyvale startup, has raised more than $100M in Series C funding.
Kevin Pope succeeds Marco Chisari as Avicena's chief executive.
InterVest led the round, Avicena announced on Tuesday.
Other investors include Tiger Global, Cerberus Capital Management, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund and AMD Ventures.
Avicena's LightBundle platform uses dense arrays of microLEDs and silicon photodetectors linked by multicore fibre.
Avicena says copper links face limits on reach, density and energy use.
Avicena says its platform spreads data across many slower channels rather than pushing a few channels very fast.
Avicena began shipping 1Tbps LightBundle evaluation kits in August.
The company plans to bring its first product to market next year.
Pope said the funding will go on hiring, product development and engineering.

context: Avicena is a Sunnyvale startup developing optical interconnects, which are links that carry data using light rather than electrical signals over copper wire. AI accelerator chips, memory and networking switches must exchange large volumes of data, and copper connections become limited in distance, density and energy efficiency. MicroLEDs are tiny light-emitting diodes that can serve as light sources in such links.
why_it_matters: The funding and product plans suggest a possible alternative to copper and laser-based links for AI hardware makers. The sources say investors including memory and chip companies see a role for the technology in memory interconnects.
open_questions: How the LightBundle product will perform once it reaches market next year is not stated in the sources.
The sources do not say what share of the round each investor contributed.

headline: AI shopping bots from Google, Amazon, Meta and OpenAI face holiday test
Los Angeles blocks AI features as Google threatens schools' search access
BharatGen launches open-weight Patram 1.5 document AI model

facts.text: BharatGen launched Patram 1.5, a seven-billion-parameter vision-language model, on November 26.
Patram 1.5 analyses documents as images rather than relying on OCR to convert pages into text first.
The launch introduces what BharatGen calls OCR 3.0, which lets users extract specific information by giving plain-language instructions.
The model is trained to flag blank or illegible fields rather than presenting an unverified answer as fact.
Patram 1.5 was evaluated across 49 tests against 20 other AI models and seven specialist OCR systems.
Patram 1.5 is available as open weights on Hugging Face and through the BharatGen Playground.
Banks, hospitals and government departments can deploy the model on their own infrastructure to process sensitive documents without sending them outside their systems.
PatramBench, BharatGen's own benchmark, was built from 8,773 pages of Indian documents and contains 11,828 test items; BharatGen said it will be released on Hugging Face in the coming days.
BharatGen CEO Rishi Bal said a model alone can only go so far and that the Playground offers a full stack for document intelligence.

context: BharatGen is a not-for-profit AI company anchored at IIT Bombay with a consortium of academic institutions, backed by the Department of Science and Technology and the IndiaAI Mission under MeitY. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is technology that converts scanned pages into machine-readable text. Open-weight models publish their trained parameters so others can download and run them.
why_it_matters: Banks, insurers, hospitals and government offices handle messy Indian paperwork such as KYC submissions, bank statements and medical reports, where errors are costly. The model aims to reduce those errors by flagging missing or unreadable data and can run on an organisation's own servers to keep sensitive files private.
open_questions: Release timing of the PatramBench benchmark, which BharatGen said would come in the coming days.
Digitisation, translation and editing features in the Playground, which are expected soon but not yet available.

headline: Backlash over AI power costs threatens $67bn NextEra-Dominion deal
Senate passes permitting bill that would speed both clean and fossil energy projects

facts.text: The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act by a 62 to 33 vote.
The bill would streamline permitting for energy and infrastructure projects, including both clean and fossil energy.
The bill was co-written by Democratic Senators Martin Heinrich and Sheldon Whitehouse and Republican Senators Mike Lee and Shelley Moore Capito.
The House of Representatives will now take up the legislation.
The bill would also ease permitting for fossil-fueled power plants, pipelines, and data centers.
Rhodium Group has found the bill would cause greenhouse gas emissions to fall, while other modelers found it could cause emissions to rise.
The Sierra Club and the Natural Resources Defense Council have come out against the legislation.
Most Democratic senators ultimately voted against the bill.
This is the first time in recent years that a permitting reform bill has passed the Senate.

context: Permitting is the government approval process that energy, transmission and infrastructure projects must clear before construction, often involving environmental reviews under laws such as NEPA and the Clean Water Act. Transmission lines carry electricity from power plants to users and are widely seen as slow to build in the US. Data centers are large facilities that consume significant electricity.
why_it_matters: Supporters say faster permitting is needed to build transmission and clean energy, while opponents, including environmental groups and some tribal groups, say the bill favors fossil fuel and data center projects and weakens environmental protections. Communities and Tribes are among those whose input the critics say would be reduced.
open_questions: Whether the House will pass the bill, where Republicans hold a slim majority.
Whether the bill's effect on emissions will increase or decrease, given conflicting model results.
Whether permitting reform will be taken up again in 2027 under a Democratic-led Congress.

headline: PJM proposes plan to regulators to cut wait times for data center power
Japan's JERA in talks with Anthropic, Meta to build data centers beside its power plants

facts.text: JERA, Japan's largest power generator, is in talks with several American tech companies about data center sites next to its power plants in the greater Tokyo area.
According to Nikkei, the talks include Anthropic and Meta.
JERA Chairman and Global CEO Yukio Kani said in an interview that Amazon, Microsoft and Google are also among the parties in discussions.
The capacity, lease timeline and contract terms under discussion with each company have not been disclosed.
It could not be confirmed whether the talks relate to the first Chiba project.
In October, JERA signed memorandums of understanding with Dell Technologies and AI infrastructure developer RHAELM for a first project at the Chiba Thermal Power Station.
The Chiba project plans power supply capacity of up to 400MW and a target launch around 2028.
JERA estimates total investment across the stages of the Chiba project will exceed $15 billion.
JERA intends to make its power supply, cooling and computing equipment model a replicable standard design and is evaluating applying it to other thermal power plants in Japan.
The source states the talks have not yet reached the signing stage.

context: JERA is a Japanese power generator formed as a 50-50 joint venture between Tokyo Electric Power (TEPCO) and Chubu Electric Power. Data centers typically must wait for substations and transmission lines before connecting to the public grid, which can delay launch. Building a data center beside an existing power plant and supplying it directly can shorten that wait.
why_it_matters: The story suggests AI computing demand is shifting the bottleneck from chips to power, and could turn Japan's thermal power plants into AI infrastructure sites. Power generators like JERA could expand from selling electricity to developing infrastructure, and the tech companies involved would gain faster access to power.
open_questions: Which companies will sign power supply contracts, and when.
Whether the Chiba project can deliver power on schedule in 2028.
Whether the replicable design can be rolled out to other power plants.
Whether the talks with Anthropic and Meta relate to the Chiba project.

headline: Britain's grid operator makes record calls for extra power in cold snap
Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
US chip export curbs: Nvidia pauses server shipments to Southeast Asia; Fitch sees slower Asia data-center investment

facts.text: Nvidia has ordered its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia.
The Financial Times reported that Nvidia told manufacturing partners to stop server shipments while it assesses compliance with the new controls.
It is unclear whether the shipment halt is temporary.
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry & Security issued the new rule on November 16, requiring licenses for advanced semiconductor exports to several countries.
The rule covers Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, which the government deems to present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.
Fitch Ratings said Asia-Pacific data-center investment will slow and become more selective because of tighter US chip controls.
The new rules took effect November 19 and require licenses for covered chip shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and Thailand.
The rule was issued after fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission that he had an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, according to DatacenterDynamics.
The US government added Singapore-based Megaspeed, along with its Thai and Malaysian subsidiaries, to the Commerce Department's Entity List.
Fitch's statement came a day after S&P placed Nvidia's rating on downgrade watch over governance concerns.

context: Nvidia designs the graphics processors (GPUs) used to train and run AI systems, and its partners such as Dell and Supermicro assemble them into servers. Export licenses are government permissions required before advanced chips can be shipped or accessed abroad. Fitch Ratings is a credit rating agency that assesses the financial strength of companies and projects.
why_it_matters: The rules could slow AI data-center construction in Southeast Asia and affect operators that serve Chinese customers, including neocloud providers and developers of nearly finished projects. Fitch says lenders may tighten financing for projects with uncertain chip supplies.
open_questions: Whether Nvidia's halt on server shipments to the four countries is temporary.
How long it will take Nvidia to complete its compliance assessment under the new controls.
Whether Moonshot AI and Z.AI model development will be delayed if overseas computing access is cut off.

headline: Ohio approves gas plant for data centers despite local voter backlash

facts.text: Ohio regulators approved construction of an 800-megawatt gas plant to power a data center complex in the central Ohio village of Ashville.
The approval came from the Ohio Power Siting Board, which found the developer met a statutory requirement that the project is in the public interest.
Ashville voters rejected the local government's agreement with developer EdgeConneX, with 81% opposing it on Election Day.
Ashville's Village Council passed a resolution in April backing the project after EdgeConneX agreed to pay up to $102 million to support municipal, school, and community work.
The gas plant will not be connected to the wider grid and will serve only the computing warehouses.
State Representative Tristan Rader, a Democrat, criticized the decision, calling the treatment of fossil fuels and renewables in Ohio a huge double standard.
Regulators said they have authority to issue the permit regardless of the election outcome, and that agreed conditions were enough to address public concerns.
The developer chose reciprocating engines and simple-cycle turbines rather than less-polluting combined-cycle turbines or fuel cells, which are more expensive right now.
The board decided the project meets the minimal environmental impact requirement, leaving air permits to the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency's expected issuance.
Critics such as Ohio Environmental Council general counsel Chris Tavenor say the board has denied renewable projects with less significant opposition, calling its approach hypocrisy.

context: The Ohio Power Siting Board is the state body that reviews and permits large energy facilities. Data centers are warehouses of computing equipment that require large amounts of electricity, and some developers are building gas-fired generation to supply them directly. Permit decisions can be challenged through rehearing requests and then appeals to the state supreme court.
why_it_matters: The decision lets a gas plant proceed next to homes, a playground, park and soccer field in Ashville despite local voter opposition, which critics say reflects a double standard against renewable projects. It also signals how state regulators weigh local government support against public votes.
open_questions: Whether opponents will request reconsideration of the ruling within the 30-day window.
Whether an appeal to the Ohio Supreme Court will follow.
Whether the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency will issue the expected air permits for the facility.

headline: Google bets on superhot geothermal to power Oregon data centers

facts.text: Houston-based geothermal startup Quaise Energy announced that Google agreed to buy 50 megawatts of carbon-free power from its Project Obsidian.
Project Obsidian is located near the Newberry Volcano in central Oregon.
Google said it plans to use the energy to help run its existing data center operations in northwest Oregon as early as 2030.
Quaise confirmed the deal is valued at more than $500 million.
Quaise is working to find offtakers for an additional 200 MW of future capacity at the Oregon site.
Quaise CEO Carlos Araque said the agreement is a critical next step for Quaise and the clean energy sector.
Quaise says the Oregon project will cost about $350 million to build.
Quaise plans to use conventional drilling first, then switch to millimeter-wave drilling to reach superhot rock above 572 degrees Fahrenheit.
Quaise is still testing the technology it plans to deploy for the Google-backed plant; it is working to drill to over 3,200 feet at its Texas field site.

context: Geothermal energy taps heat from underground to generate electricity. Conventional plants use naturally hot reservoirs, while enhanced geothermal systems fracture rock and pump water through it to create reservoirs. Superhot geothermal aims to drill much deeper into hotter rock to extract more energy from fewer wells.
why_it_matters: The deal gives a startup a major customer for clean, around-the-clock power, which helps it raise the financing needed to build first-of-a-kind geothermal plants. Tech companies such as Google, which need steady clean power for data centers, are among those affected.
open_questions: The sources say the technology has yet to be deployed widely at commercial scale.
Questions remain about how well the plants will operate over long periods.
The 200 MW of additional capacity still needs offtakers.

headline: Norway pauses data center grid connections as requests outgrow its power system

facts.text: Statnett, Norway's transmission system operator, paused new grid reservations for data centers on 9 November.
The same day, the government announced a licensing scheme that will keep out new crypto mining.
The grid reservation halt will last until at least August 2027, when a new system is set to come into effect.
Data centers have requested about 34 GW of grid capacity in Norway, well above national peak demand of about 25 GW.
Only 0.8 GW of data center capacity is connected to the grid in Norway today.
Statnett has stopped granting new reservations and approving facility functionality while it sets functional requirements for data centers.
Projects with reserved capacity keep their place but still need approval before connecting, and existing connections are not affected.
Norway has six operating crypto data centers with about 0.2 GW combined, and new crypto sites will not be permitted under the licensing scheme.
Under normal hydrology, rising demand could cut Norway's net exports by 71%, from 14.3 TWh in 2027 to 4.1 TWh in 2030, according to Rystad's analysis.
In a dry year, Norway could become a net importer and winter prices could reach about €290 per megawatt-hour.

context: Statnett is Norway's state-owned transmission system operator, responsible for the high-voltage grid that moves electricity across the country. A grid reservation is a place in the queue for a connection to that network, so pausing reservations means new projects cannot secure a spot. Norway gets most of its electricity from hydropower and has long had a power surplus that kept prices low.
why_it_matters: The pause affects data center developers seeking new grid connections, who must wait until at least August 2027 for new reservations. The analysis suggests rising data center demand could erode Norway's power surplus and export income, potentially pushing up electricity prices for households and industry.
open_questions: When the new grid system takes effect in August 2027 and what its final rules will be.
How the functional requirements for data centers will be set and what they will specifically require.
Whether gas power with carbon capture and storage or offshore wind can be built in time to meet new demand.

headline: IAEA works with Russia, Ukraine on ceasefire to repair Zaporizhzhia power link
Massachusetts to require new data centers to use clean energy
Feds back $4B project to connect eastern and western US grids

facts.text: The U.S. Department of Energy announced federal backing for an electric power line intertie in Wyoming that will double the flow of electricity between the eastern and western grids.
Houston-based Grid United's project is estimated at $4 billion.
The project is backed by a $2.8 billion conditional loan from the federal Energy Dominance Financing program.
The line would run 106 miles from the Laramie River Station coal-fired power plant outside Wheatland to the Aeolus substation near Medicine Bow.
The connection is bidirectional, letting operators send electricity either direction between the grids.
Office of Energy Dominance Financing Director Gregory Beard said the bridging of the two systems provides more reliable energy flows and lowers ratepayer electricity bills.
Construction of the three-year intertie is expected to begin in 2030.
According to the DOE, the intertie is estimated to save ratepayers in Wyoming and 17 other states a combined $39 billion in avoided costs over 30 years.
Wyoming Energy Authority official John Jenks cautioned that the intertie won't necessarily lower rates for Wyoming customers.
According to Beard, about 90% of the route consists of state and federally owned land, and the project may receive fast-track permitting.
Grid United says it is still working with tribal nations and landowners to finalize the route, which remains proposed until county, state and federal approval.

context: The eastern and western U.S. electric grids are two largely separate systems that are only weakly connected, so power generally cannot move easily between them. An intertie is a transmission line that links two grids, allowing electricity to be shared across them. Laramie River Station is a coal-fired power plant in Wyoming, one of the few plants with access to both grids.
why_it_matters: The line would let electricity move in either direction between the eastern and western grids, which the DOE says could help during demand surges, outages and extreme weather. Wyoming ratepayers and residents of 17 other states would be affected, though the state's energy official said lower bills are a theory rather than a sure outcome.
open_questions: Whether the conditional loan will be finalized is not stated.
The final route is still being finalized with tribal nations and landowners.
The project still needs approval from county, state and federal regulators before construction can begin.
Whether fast-track permitting will be granted is not yet decided.

headline: Nuclear plants to stay open longer as new builds hit delays and costs
Taiwan votes on nuclear power as AI boom revives debate

facts.text: Taiwan holds a national referendum on abolishing its denuclearization-first policy alongside local elections on the 28th.
The referendum question asks whether the government should revitalize the economy through nuclear power and abolish the denuclearization-first energy policy.
The opposition Kuomintang proposed the referendum, the People's Party supports it, and the ruling Democratic Progressive Party opposes it.
This is the fourth national referendum related to nuclear power since 2018.
Supporters argue nuclear power is needed as a stable low-carbon source for the growing electricity demand of semiconductor and artificial intelligence industries.
Opponents say there is no plan for nuclear waste disposal and that earthquake risks and electricity costs must be considered.
To pass, the referendum needs more yes votes than no votes and at least one-quarter of all voters, about 5,000,959 votes of 20,003,835 registered voters.
Last year a proposal to restart the third nuclear power plant was rejected for falling short of the required yes votes, with 4.341 million in favor and 1.512 million against.
Even if the referendum passes, nuclear plants will not immediately resume operation, and abolishing the non-nuclear clause requires legislative amendment.
Opponents at a Taipei rally urged voters to vote no, arguing all four nuclear plants sit near geological fault lines that may not withstand strong earthquakes.
Taiwan Environmental Protection Union president Hsieh Chih-cheng said zero nuclear use over 532 days did not cause a power shortage, with 501 days having reserve margins above 10 percent.

context: Taiwan adopted a Denuclearization Initiative under its Framework Act on the Environment in 2002, aiming to phase out nuclear power and replace it with natural gas and renewables. Referendums in Taiwan are binding only in limited ways and require both a majority of yes votes and a minimum turnout threshold to pass.
why_it_matters: The vote could reshape Taiwan's long-term energy policy at a time when AI and semiconductor industries are driving rising electricity demand. Voters, the government and power companies would all be affected by the outcome.
open_questions: Whether the referendum's legal effect will be clear, since the sources say the questions lack specific content.
Whether the third nuclear plant will be restarted, which depends on Taiwan Power Company's safety assessment and operating license rather than the referendum.

headline: Vietnam weighs delaying nuclear plants beyond 2035 target

facts.text: Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade has proposed a 2037 or 2038 start date for the Ninh Thuan 1 nuclear plant.
The Ministry proposed 2039 or 2040 as the start date for Ninh Thuan 2.
The proposals appear in a draft revision to the nation's power development plan published for consultation.
The existing plan called for Ninh Thuan 1 to become operational between 2030 and 2035.
Planners, including Russian partner Rosatom, assess that at least 12 years are needed to build the project once a feasibility study is completed.
EVN still proposes an earlier completion of 2034 or 2035 for Ninh Thuan 1 if conditions are favourable.
Vietnam Electricity Group (EVN) has submitted a pre-feasibility study for Ninh Thuan 1 to the finance ministry.
The revised plan also cuts LNG-fired power capacity to about 4.3 gigawatts by 2030, less than half the existing plan's figure.
The revised plan scraps the addition of about six gigawatts of offshore wind capacity by 2030, while solar capacity is expected to rise to 81.6 GW.
The Ministry of Industry and Trade has not said when it will make a final decision on the plan.

context: Nuclear power plants are large facilities that generate electricity from nuclear fission, and they typically take many years to plan, finance and build. Vietnam has been pursuing nuclear power to reduce its dependence on imported fossil fuels. Vietnam Electricity Group (EVN) is a state-owned utility, and Rosatom is Russia's state nuclear corporation, the technology partner for Ninh Thuan 1.
why_it_matters: Delays push back when Vietnam can add nuclear capacity, which clouds its effort to cut reliance on imported fossil fuels, a vulnerability highlighted by soaring energy prices this year. The revised plan also affects LNG and offshore wind projects.
open_questions: When the Ministry of Industry and Trade will make a final decision on the revised plan is not yet known.
Whether EVN's earlier 2034-2035 timeline for Ninh Thuan 1 will be met depends on favourable mechanisms and policies not yet in place.
The timeline for Ninh Thuan 2 under its earlier 2035-2036 proposal is conditional and not yet decided.

headline: Rest of world plays catch-up with China's solar dominance as Chinese turbine makers go abroad
Trump EPA keeps trying to kill Solar for All despite court losses

facts.text: The Trump administration appealed a court ruling that sought to restore the Solar for All program.
Solar for All was first envisioned in 2022 as part of the Inflation Reduction Act.
In 2024 the EPA picked winners who would split a $7 billion pot to expand solar access for low-income and disadvantaged households.
In August 2025 the EPA announced it was killing Solar for All.
Advocates, solar installers, and a labor group challenged the EPA's decision in court.
A federal judge ruled in September that the EPA's rollback was illegal and its reasoning for terminating the program was unjustified.
A second judge later ruled in favor of protecting Solar for All.
The EPA has never resumed grant payments under the program.
The NRDC's Adam Kent said the administration is continuing its obstruction and delay of the program.
Six Republican members of Congress wrote to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin urging the EPA to reinstate the program.

context: Solar for All is a federal program created under the Inflation Reduction Act to fund solar power access for low-income and disadvantaged households. The EPA, the Environmental Protection Agency, administers the grants that states, local governments, tribes, territories and nonprofits receive. Grant recipients were developing community solar, rooftop solar and battery storage projects before the program was cancelled.
why_it_matters: The dispute determines whether funded community solar and battery projects for low-income households can proceed, affecting grant recipients and the households they serve. Advocates and some Republican lawmakers argue the program could lower energy bills.
open_questions: Whether the appeals court will reverse the ruling restoring Solar for All.
Whether the EPA will resume grant payments under the program.
The outcome of some ongoing lawsuits seeking to recover individual grants.

headline: China's nuclear buildout advances: Tianwan 8 fuel load, Fuqing 6 in service, Taishan 3 construction

facts.text: TVEL, Rosatom's fuel division, supplied fuel for Tianwan unit 8, a VVER-1200 reactor in Jiangsu Province.
The fuel delivery includes the initial core load and a reserve batch of fuel assemblies.
China National Nuclear Power said it successfully completed hot tests at the new Tianwan unit on a Wednesday.
Hot tests aim to verify the reliability of equipment in the nuclear and conventional parts of the plant.
Once unit 8 is operational, Tianwan will have about 9.1 GW of installed capacity, making it the world's largest nuclear power plant by capacity.
Fuqing unit 6, a Hualong One demonstration reactor, entered commercial operation on a Friday, according to CNNC.
Fuqing unit 6 is the second Chinese Hualong One reactor in operation in China and the third in the world.
Fuqing unit 6 reached first criticality on December 11 and full power on February 19.
Taishan unit 3 in Guangdong Province entered construction after first concrete was poured for its nuclear island on November 25, 2026, according to the construction-start report.
Taishan unit 3 is a roughly 1,200 MW Hualong One reactor being developed by CGN.
CGN has not announced a confirmed commercial operation date or total investment for Taishan unit 3.

context: Tianwan, Fuqing and Taishan are nuclear power plants in southern and eastern China, operated by state-linked utilities such as CNNC and CGN. Hot tests simulate the temperatures and pressures a reactor will face in normal operation, while fuel loading and first criticality mark the stages before a reactor begins commercial power generation. Hualong One is China's domestically developed third-generation pressurised water reactor design.
why_it_matters: These milestones add generating capacity to China's grid and expand its low-carbon electricity supply, benefiting Jiangsu, Fujian and Guangdong regions that the plants serve. Tianwan's completion would make it the largest nuclear plant in the world by installed capacity.
open_questions: When unit 8 at Tianwan will enter commercial operation is not stated in the sources.
The commercial operation date for Taishan unit 3 has not been announced.
The sources do not give a date for the Tianwan unit 8 hot test completion beyond 'Wednesday'.

headline: Avantus signs PG&E PPAs for 800 MW solar and 3,200 MWh storage

facts.text: Avantus signed 20-year power purchase agreements with Pacific Gas and Electric for the Buttonbush 1A and 1B projects in Kern County, California.
Buttonbush 1A and 1B together add up to 800 MW of solar and 3,200 MWh of battery storage.
The estimated build cost is $3 billion, according to the announcement.
Avantus says the combined output is enough to power approximately 381,000 homes each year.
Regulators must approve the agreements, and power delivery is due in 2029.
Avantus estimates the projects will produce hundreds of millions of dollars in local property taxes over their operating life.
PG&E's Gillian Clegg said the projects will be among the largest clean energy resources in the utility's portfolio.
Avantus CEO Cliff Graham said Buttonbush would keep low-cost solar flowing into the evening, when demand peaks.
Avantus intends to keep ownership of Buttonbush 1A and 1B and operate both projects itself as an independent power producer.

context: Power purchase agreements (PPAs) are long-term contracts in which a utility agrees to buy electricity from a power producer at set terms. Utility-scale solar pairs large solar farms with battery storage, which stores daytime power for use in the evening when demand is high. Kern County is an agricultural region in California's Central Valley.
why_it_matters: The contracts lock in roughly 20 years of solar-plus-storage output for PG&E's customers, with the evening power supply and fixed pricing that the sources describe as the main purpose. Local landowners, workers and county tax revenue are also affected, according to the sources.
open_questions: Regulators must still approve the PG&E agreements.
The announcement gives battery storage in megawatt-hours but not the batteries' power rating in megawatts.

headline: Japan's METI awards Kyoto Fusioneering-led group up to JPY 23.3bn for tokamak demo

facts.text: Japan's METI formally confirmed a subsidy award of up to JPY 23.3 billion (about $146.3 million) to a consortium led by Starlight Engine, a group company of Kyoto Fusioneering.
The grant funds a fusion power generation demonstration project running from fiscal year 2026 through 2028.
The project aims to demonstrate actual power generation from fusion energy using a tokamak device with high-temperature superconducting coils.
The formal selection was announced in November 2026, following a conditional selection announced on August 31, 2026.
The consortium's work is meant to mature engineering technologies ahead of a power generation demonstration at the FAST plant in the 2030s.

The three-year work spans 10 engineering areas, including plant integration, coils, divertor, heating, fuel, blanket, remote maintenance, materials, activated materials handling, and diagnostics and control.
The funding comes through METI's FY2025 Supplementary Budget.
Kyoto Fusioneering appointed Pattrick Calderoni, former fusion program lead at Idaho National Laboratory, as Director of Blanket Programs, announced November 20, 2026.
Calderoni will serve as co-Chief Scientist for UNITY-3, a 14 MeV blanket test facility Kyoto Fusioneering is developing with Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

context: METI is Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, which funds strategic technologies through its budgets. Kyoto Fusioneering is a private company focused on commercializing fusion energy. A tokamak is a doughnut-shaped magnetic device used to confine hot plasma for fusion, and high-temperature superconducting coils generate strong magnetic fields.
why_it_matters: The award gives public money to a private-sector consortium aiming to show fusion-generated electricity at the FAST plant within the decade, signaling government backing for the technology. Japan's fusion industry and energy planners are the parties most directly affected by the funding.
open_questions: Whether the FAST plant will achieve fusion-generated electricity in the 2030s is not yet known.
The sources do not detail how the three-year design and component work will translate into the later demonstration phase.

headline: Wyoming grid expansion for Microsoft data centers

facts.text: Cheyenne Light submitted an application to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to build transmission and distribution infrastructure to power three planned Microsoft data centers.
Microsoft will foot the bill for the infrastructure, paying through a contribution in aid of construction and an up-front payment.
The filed agreements are redacted, so the size and terms of the deal are not publicly available.
Cheyenne Light said FERC does not have jurisdiction over the retail agreements with Microsoft but filed the application out of an abundance of caution.
Cheyenne Light is a subsidiary of Bright Horizon Energy, formed through a merger of Black Hills Corp. and NorthWestern Energy Group.
Bright Horizon is advancing two transmission projects in Wyoming with an estimated combined investment of $686 million.
The $686 million figure covers wider transmission investment and does not represent the construction cost of Microsoft's three data centers.
The Aeolus Transmission Project is estimated at $606 million and includes two 230-kilovolt lines spanning about 125 miles.
Both transmission projects require approval from the Wyoming Public Service Commission, with regulatory decisions expected around mid-2027.
Cheyenne Light plans to serve the data centers under its large load tariff.

context: Cheyenne Light is a Wyoming electric utility that delivers power to customers around Cheyenne. Transmission lines carry high-voltage electricity from generation sources to substations, while distribution lines deliver it to end users. A contribution in aid of construction is a payment by a customer that covers the cost of building utility infrastructure for it.
why_it_matters: The arrangement puts the cost of new power infrastructure for Microsoft's Cheyenne data centers on Microsoft rather than other electricity customers, which the utility says is intended to protect ratepayers. It also signals continued growth of data center demand in southeast Wyoming.
open_questions: What are the size and terms of the Microsoft agreements, which remain redacted?
Will the Wyoming Public Service Commission approve the two transmission projects, expected around mid-2027?
Whether FERC has jurisdiction over the Microsoft agreements is not settled, since Cheyenne Light says it filed only as a precaution.

headline: Japan nuclear restart hit by delay at Kashiwazaki Kariwa-7

facts.text: Tokyo Electric Power Company (Tepco) said the restart of Unit 7 at Kashiwazaki Kariwa will be delayed by more than one year.
The delay is caused by setbacks to a mandatory counterterrorism facility at the plant.
Tepco had hoped to complete the counterterrorism facility by August 2029, but work is behind schedule.
Takeyuki Inagaki, head of the plant, said the target for completing the facility is now April 2031.
The announcement was made on Thursday, 26 November, at a press conference.
Kashiwazaki Kariwa is located in Niigata Prefecture, western Japan.

context: Kashiwazaki Kariwa is a nuclear power station in Niigata Prefecture, Japan, operated by Tokyo Electric Power Company (Tepco).
