Japan's nuclear restart programme involves bringing reactors that were shut down after the 2011 Fukushima accident back into operation, which requires safety reviews and related facilities. A mandatory counterterrorism facility is a required security installation at a nuclear plant.
why_it_matters: The delay pushes back the restart of Unit 7 at Kashiwazaki Kariwa by more than a year, affecting Tepco's plans for the plant and the wider nuclear restart programme in Japan.
open_questions: Whether the new April 2031 completion target for the counterterrorism facility will be met.

headline: Sabah power outage after Ranau tower collapse; restoration targeted Dec 2

facts.text: Transmission tower T313 in Ranau collapsed, detected at 6.04am on the day before the reports.
The collapse severed two transmission line circuits carrying power from Sabah's West Coast to its East Coast.
The outage disrupted electricity supply across eight districts and affected 153,599 registered consumers.
Sabah Electricity has set a six-day timeframe to restore the 275-kV transmission line, targeting full grid restoration by Dec 2.
Sabah Electricity Chairman Datuk Saadiah Aziz said the company is targeting a six-day period to reconnect the grid, which could possibly be completed even earlier.
The Emergency Restoration System (ERS) temporary tower components arrived at the Ranau collapse site on Nov 27.
The lorry carrying the ERS temporary tower container arrived at the site of tower T313 at 1.07am.

Electricity on the East Coast is being generated by existing power plants in Sandakan and Tawau, supported by portable or mobile generators, with the Tawau station supplying power while Sandakan is still being restored.
Load-shedding is limited to one to two hours, with rotational rationing due to limited local generation capacity.
Sabah Electricity said viral messages claiming a two-week outage across the entire East Coast are fake.
MCMC is coordinating telecommunications restoration after 1,196 cellular sites were affected and fixed lines disrupted.

context: Sabah Electricity is the state utility supplying power in Malaysia's Sabah region. The 275-kV transmission line is a high-voltage link that carries bulk power between the West and East Coasts of Sabah. A transmission tower is the steel structure holding these high-voltage lines, and temporary emergency towers can be installed to restore a severed line quickly.
why_it_matters: Around 153,599 consumers across eight districts on Sabah's East Coast lost supply, and local plants are carrying the load with rationing and generators. Hospitals, schools and police stations are being kept supplied by portable generators.
open_questions: Whether full grid restoration will be completed by Dec 2 as targeted.
Whether the Sandakan station will be fully restored.

headline: Malaysia's electricity demand set to double by 2050 on data centers

facts.text: Electricity demand in Peninsular Malaysia is expected to more than double by 2050, rising from 22.6 GW in 2027 to 49.8 GW.
The forecast was shared by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra) and implies a compound annual growth rate of about 3.5%.
The projection accounts for rapid expansion of data centres, artificial intelligence, electric vehicles and energy-intensive industries.
Data centres' share of Peninsular Malaysia's total demand is projected to rise from 11% in 2027 to 21% by 2050.
Malaysia is considering nuclear energy as a potential baseload source alongside natural gas, to meet demand while supporting its net-zero target by 2050.
According to Petra, an initial scenario discussed at JPPPET Meeting No. 1/2026 anticipates possible introduction of nuclear energy from 2040.
Nuclear power could account for about 2% of the generation mix, around 2.0 GW, before 2050.
Final nuclear capacity depends on a comprehensive feasibility study being conducted by MyPOWER, the agency implementing the nuclear programme.
Terengganu, Kelantan and Perlis together have 25 large-scale solar projects totalling 1,531 MW, or 25.4% of Malaysia's 6,028 MW LSS capacity.
Petra said the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) follows a willing buyer, willing seller approach, and developers are not restricted to particular states.

entities: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra)
Electricity Supply and Tariff Planning and Implementation Committee (JPPPET)
context: Peninsular Malaysia is the western part of the country, where most of its electricity is consumed. Petra is the government ministry responsible for energy transition and water policy, and JPPPET is the committee that produces electricity supply and tariff planning estimates. Large-scale solar (LSS) refers to utility-scale solar power plants feeding the grid.
why_it_matters: The forecast signals a sharp rise in power needs driven largely by data centres, which could shape how Malaysia builds generation capacity and grid infrastructure. The move toward nuclear and expanded solar affects energy planning for the country's future electricity supply.
open_questions: Final nuclear capacity and contribution depend on the MyPOWER feasibility study, which is not yet complete.
The source does not say which specific technology or site would be used for nuclear power.

headline: XPeng unveils Turing physical AI architecture (VLA 3.0) and IRON humanoid, targeting mass production in January 2027

facts.text: XPeng unveiled its IRON general-purpose humanoid robot at its AI Day 2026 in Guangzhou, China.
XPeng describes its Turing Physical AI architecture as VLA 3.0, built from three systems operating at different speeds.
XPeng says hardware mass production of IRON is scheduled to begin in January 2027.
XPeng says IRON is scheduled to begin training as a store assistant in its retail stores in Q1 2027.
The latest IRON has 76 degrees of freedom, including a 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand and more than 1,500 tactile sensing points.
XPeng says its automated humanoid production line is designed to complete one IRON every 2.5 minutes at full capacity.
XPeng's CEO He Xiaopeng said robots need hardware first, and that the industry must prove robots can create value in the real world.
A Supercar Blondie report says IRON was unveiled on stage and told the audience it was a little nervous.
The Supercar Blondie report says the 2026 IRON will go into mass production next year, and it does not state a sales date or price.

context: XPeng is a Chinese electric vehicle and physical AI company listed on the NYSE and HKEX. A humanoid robot is a general-purpose robot with a human-like body that is designed to perform varied tasks. VLA stands for vision-language-action, a type of AI model that links what a robot sees and understands to physical movement.
why_it_matters: XPeng is positioning IRON as a commercial work robot, starting with retail store roles before expanding to industrial and home uses. If the January 2027 mass production target holds, it would be an early step toward humanoid robots moving beyond demonstrations.
open_questions: Whether the January 2027 mass production target will be met.
How IRON performs in real-world working environments beyond polished demos, according to a YouTuber who interacted with it at the event.

headline: Nvidia forecasts physical AI revenue above $25 billion in fiscal 2027

facts.text: Nvidia expects physical AI revenue to exceed $25 billion in fiscal 2027.
The forecast was presented on Nvidia's third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call on November 17, 2026.
The fiscal year ends in late January 2027.
Nvidia does not report physical AI as a separate business segment.
The physical AI products include the Isaac robotics platform, which trains and simulates robots, and Jetson and Thor onboard computers that run AI locally.
In the quarter, Nvidia posted total revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier.
Data Center revenue rose 110% to $107.6 billion in the quarter.
Nvidia raised its fiscal 2028 revenue-growth outlook to approximately 75%, from an earlier estimate of 70%.
Colette Kress, interim CEO and CFO, ran the earnings call.

context: Physical AI refers to artificial intelligence that operates in the real world, such as robots on factory floors, self-driving cars and industrial systems. Nvidia is a chipmaker best known for supplying the processors used in AI data centers. Its Isaac platform helps developers train and simulate robots, while Jetson and Thor are onboard computers that run AI on the machine itself.
why_it_matters: The forecast suggests Nvidia may diversify beyond its data center business, which depends heavily on a small group of large buyers building AI infrastructure. Investors are watching whether this new business grows as projected.
open_questions: Whether physical AI revenue actually exceeds $25 billion when full-year results are released after the fiscal year ends in late January 2027.
Whether Nvidia will begin reporting physical AI as a standalone segment.
Whether the raised fiscal 2028 growth target of approximately 75% will hold.

headline: Volvo Cars begins training Hexagon AEON humanoids at Ghent plant ahead of 2027 rollout

facts.text: Volvo Cars has begun training Hexagon Robotics' AEON humanoid robots at its plant in Ghent, Belgium.
Ghent is the first Volvo Cars plant to try humanoid robots, the company said.
The robots are learning through imitation learning, copying how people perform tasks.
The first task is placing components into two fixtures with high precision.
Additional AEON units are scheduled to arrive in Ghent for a factory pilot in the first half of 2027.
Volvo plans for the robots to begin working in regular production from mid-2027.
AEON is 1.65 meters tall, weighs 60 kilograms, moves on wheels and can carry up to 10 kilograms.
Volvo did not say how many robots are at the plant now or how many will join the pilot.
Volvo's chief manufacturing officer Magnus Nilsson said AEON's design lets it fit into production as it is today.

context: Volvo Cars is a Swedish carmaker, and Hexagon Robotics is a division of Sweden's Hexagon technology group. Imitation learning is a training method in which a robot learns a task by copying a human performing it. Humanoid robots are human-shaped machines, and AEON is designed to do different jobs in existing factories, unlike fixed industrial robot arms.
why_it_matters: The trial is an early test of whether humanoid robots can take on physically demanding, repetitive factory work at a car plant. Volvo says the robots are meant to support employees and make work more ergonomic.
open_questions: How many AEON robots will join the factory pilot in 2027 is not stated.
Whether the pilot will lead to wider use in Volvo's vehicle production is not yet decided.

headline: XPeng says IRON humanoid will cost about as much as an EV and could do household chores in 1-2 years

facts.text: XPeng says its IRON humanoid robot could retail near the average selling price of its vehicles.
XPeng's electric vehicles retail from about 119,800 yuan to 309,800 yuan, roughly $18,000 at the low end.
Vice-Chairman Brian Gu said in a Bloomberg TV interview that IRON units could be priced around the median selling price for an EV.
XPeng plans to train IRON as a training assistant in its own retail stores in the first quarter of 2027.
XPeng plans to open public sales of IRON in the second quarter of 2027, with deliveries expected later that year.
Gu did not provide a specific final price for the robot beyond pointing to the EV median price level.
Gu said household deployment would likely follow one to two years after a successful commercial rollout.
Gu cited safety around children, the elderly and pets, plus emergency response, as raising the bar for home use.
XPeng has set a target of selling tens of thousands of humanoid robots next year.
IRON was unveiled at XPeng's AI Day event in Guangzhou, where it was shown interacting with an attendee on Nov. 25.

context: XPeng is a Chinese automaker that makes electric vehicles and is now developing humanoid robots. A humanoid robot is a machine built with a human-like body and general-purpose AI, intended to perform tasks such as guiding visitors or doing chores. Comparing a robot's price to an EV's price gives listeners a rough sense of cost, though it is not an official price list.
why_it_matters: If XPeng delivers at an EV-level price, business buyers could consider the robot as a way to substitute for labor, while household buyers would still face a much higher cost. The sources say the pricing is only a benchmark, so buyers and investors cannot yet rely on it as a firm offer.
open_questions: What the final retail price of IRON will be, since Gu gave no specific figure.
Whether XPeng's retail training in the first quarter of 2027 will show the robot performing reliably.
When household use will actually begin, given it depends on a successful commercial rollout first.

headline: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after resignation reports; Trump says market feels good

facts.text: NVIDIA's board announced that co-founder Jensen Huang has been reinstated as company president, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
The reinstatement was announced in a press release on Monday, November 23.
Huang had resigned as president and CEO on November 12, after reports of an extramarital affair.
Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese business executive, on November 10, according to the sources.
Alice Huang is reportedly an asset of China's Ministry of State Security, according to new reports cited by the source.
Following allegations of a personal affair with a potential Chinese spy, the board formed an independent committee to investigate the allegations.
The board said the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion, and Huang fully supports it and is committed to cooperating.
During Huang's absence, Colette Kress served as interim CEO while continuing as Chief Financial Officer.
NVIDIA's stock dropped 27% in the 11 days after Huang's resignation, and the company lost over $1 trillion in market capitalization.
Harvey C. Jones, chair of the board, said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead NVIDIA.

context: NVIDIA is a technology company best known for graphics processors and chips used in AI and accelerated computing. Its board of directors oversees the company and can appoint or replace its chief executive. An independent committee is a group set up by a board, usually with outside members, to investigate a matter without management involvement.
why_it_matters: Huang's return restores NVIDIA's leadership after a period of significant market losses, affecting shareholders, employees, partners and customers. The investigation into the allegations remains ongoing and could affect the company's governance.
open_questions: What will the independent committee's investigation find, and when will it conclude?
Whether the reports that Alice Huang is linked to China's intelligence service are confirmed is not established in the sources.
The Times report about Kimberly Powell was not verified by CBS News at the time of the source article.

headline: Japan's Noetra launches with 44 companies for domestic physical AI, METI backing up to ¥1.3 trillion

facts.text: Noetra is a new company aiming to develop a Japanese-made AI foundation model to serve as the brain of robots.
Noetra began full operations in July.
SoftBank, Sony Group, Honda, NEC and 40 other Japanese companies have joined Noetra, totaling 44 companies.
Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry has indicated it will provide support totaling at least ¥1.3 trillion, roughly $8.2 billion.
Under the fiscal 2026 budget, METI will spend roughly ¥390 billion to procure about 27,500 GPUs from Nvidia for developing foundation models.
The GPUs are planned to be installed at a large data center in Sakai.
Hirotora Tamba, who became Noetra's president, met Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on the 12th to make the case for Japanese-made AI.
Daisuke Okanohara of Preferred Networks and Yoshihisa Ijiri of SoftBank's AI development subsidiary were appointed co-heads of development.
About 100 engineers have been dispatched by the participating companies to the core development work.
Some observers point to the risk that the scale of national spending will swell, and voices question the return on investment.

context: Noetra is a company formed to build a Japanese-made foundation model for physical AI, meaning AI embodied in robots that must learn from senses such as vision and touch. METI is Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, which funds and supports industrial policy. Foundation models are large general-purpose AI models that can be adapted to many tasks.
why_it_matters: The effort is Japan's bid to regain ground in physical AI after falling behind the United States and China in language models, and it affects domestic manufacturers and AI developers. Its success depends on whether Japan can reduce dependence on overseas technology.
open_questions: Whether the full ¥1.3 trillion in government support will be realized, since the figures are based on the fiscal 2026 budget proposal.
How efficiently the computing infrastructure with 27,500 GPUs can be turned into development results.
Whether Japan can make its physical AI foundation models independent of overseas technology.

headline: US investigates Waymo over school bus passing; recall covers 4,488 vehicles tied to closed-lane incidents

facts.text: Waymo's recall 26E086 covers 4,488 potentially involved fifth- and sixth-generation automated driving system units capable of operating without a driver.
The recall concerns Waymo robotaxis entering closed freeway lanes, according to Waymo's filing with NHTSA.
Waymo's filing lists 11 entries into closed freeway lanes, with no collisions or injuries reported in those events.
Waymo submitted the recall report to NHTSA on November 19, 2026, saying the final remedy was still under development.
Reuters reported on November 24 that the 11 closed-lane incidents prompted a recall covering nearly 4,500 self-driving vehicles in the United States.
Interim measures including operational controls, trip-routing changes and dynamic map changes took effect on November 11 to limit exposure to lane closures.
The US auto safety regulator NHTSA opened an investigation on November 6, 2026, into Waymo robotaxis allegedly passing stopped school buses with flashing red lights.
Motorsafety.org says a school bus investigation could affect an estimated 2,895 vehicles with the 5th generation ADS, a figure not stated in the recall filing coverage.
Waymo already recalled vehicles over the school bus issue in December 2025 and updated the software, and investigators will assess the repair's effectiveness.
The Austin Independent School District demanded that Waymo cease operations during school drop-off and pick-up hours after a late 2025 incident.
In November 2026, the California Department of Motor Vehicles banned Waymo from operating on the state's freeways after cars intruded into roadwork sections.

context: Waymo is an autonomous ride-hailing company whose robotaxis operate without a human driver. Under US law, automakers must file a recall with NHTSA, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, when a vehicle defect poses a safety risk. NHTSA can also open investigations into possible safety violations, which can lead to recalls.
why_it_matters: The stories affect riders, pedestrians and students near school zones, since the sources describe robotaxis that may pass stopped school buses or enter closed lanes. They also bear on whether driverless vehicles can be trusted to follow traffic rules in construction and school areas.
open_questions: Whether the school bus investigation will lead to a recall is not yet known.
Whether Waymo's software repair for the school bus issue is effective is for investigators to determine.
The final remedy for the closed-lane recall was still under development as of the filing.

headline: Samsung plans robots in chip fabs by 2028 and humanoid push, sparking Korean robot stock rally

facts.text: Samsung Electronics has recently set up a robotics team within its Semiconductor (DS) division.
Samsung Electronics has also set up an organization responsible for mergers and acquisitions in robotics.
Samsung Electronics identified robots and AI as future growth areas in its executive appointments for 2027 announced on November 24.
The market is watching for a possible Samsung humanoid robot showcase at CES 2027 in Las Vegas, held January 6 to 9, 2027.
Xenics Robotics shares hit the daily upper limit, rising 29.98% to 8,020 won in morning trading on the 27th.
Other robot-related stocks also rose sharply, including Rainbow Robotics up 11.56% and Cosmorobotics up 30.0%.
Eugene Investment & Securities researcher Yang Seung-yoon said Samsung is strengthening its robot transformation development organization ahead of CES 2027.
Eugene Investment & Securities estimates cumulative global humanoid robot installations will reach 7.87 million units by 2040.
Shinhan Securities initiated coverage of Hyundai AutoEver with a buy rating and a target price of 470,000 won.

context: Samsung Electronics is a large South Korean electronics and chipmaking conglomerate, and its semiconductor division runs the fabs where chips are manufactured. Humanoid robots are human-shaped machines intended for work in factories and homes. CES is a major consumer technology trade show held each January in Las Vegas, where companies often unveil new products.
why_it_matters: Investors reacted by sharply buying Korean robot-related stocks, which rose on expectations of benefits from Samsung's robotics push. The sources say the rally reflects hopes rather than confirmed product launches.
open_questions: Samsung has not yet confirmed a humanoid robot reveal at CES 2027 in the sources.
The sources do not confirm the 2028 timeline for robots in chip fabs stated in the headline.
How quickly humanoid robots will be deployed in the field remains uncertain, with the analyst projecting deployment starting in 2027.

headline: Rockwell Automation to acquire AGILOX

facts.text: Rockwell Automation has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Austria-based AGILOX.
AGILOX makes autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) driven by self-developed AI and swarm networking technology.
Terms of the acquisition, including the price, were not disclosed.
Rockwell says AGILOX's forklift AMR portfolio and OTTO's flatbed AMR platform will together create a comprehensive autonomous material movement system.
Rockwell says the deal combines OTTO's strong presence in North America with AGILOX's established footprint across Europe.
Rockwell says AGILOX will gain access to its customer relationships in consumer-packaged goods and life sciences.
Rockwell says the acquisition will more than double its AMR business.
Blake Moret, chairman and CEO of Rockwell Automation, said combining the two technologies sets a new standard for autonomous material movement.
AGILOX co-CEOs Dirk Erlacher and David Niedermaier said joining Rockwell gives AGILOX scale and market reach it could not build on its own.
The transaction is subject to closing conditions and regulatory approval, and Rockwell expects it to close in the second quarter of its fiscal year 2027.

context: Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) are self-navigating vehicles that move materials around factories and warehouses without a human driver. Forklift AMRs carry pallets, while flatbed AMRs carry loads on a flat platform. Rockwell Automation is an industrial automation company that makes factory control systems and equipment.
why_it_matters: The deal would combine Rockwell's OTTO flatbed robots with AGILOX's forklift robots into one material-movement offering, and Rockwell says it would more than double its AMR business. Customers in factories and warehouses, especially in consumer goods and life sciences, would be affected by the broader product range.
open_questions: The purchase price was not disclosed.
The deal still needs closing conditions and regulatory approval before it completes.
The exact closing date is not confirmed beyond an expected second quarter of fiscal 2027.

headline: Tesla robotaxi fleet registered in Texas edges past Waymo, with 1,000+ Cybercabs

facts.text: A Texas registry figure cited by a social media post shows 1,507 vehicles registered for Tesla versus 1,390 for Waymo.
According to the Mario Nawfal post, Tesla added around 200 Cybercabs in one batch, helping it take the lead in the state's driverless vehicle registry.

context: Waymo, owned by Alphabet, operates driverless robotaxi service and has led the autonomous ride-hailing market for years. Tesla's Cybercab is a two-seat vehicle built for driverless rides, with no steering wheel or pedals. Texas publishes a registry of vehicles authorized to operate autonomously, which is the source of the fleet counts being compared.
why_it_matters: The comparison matters to riders, investors and regulators because it tracks which company is scaling driverless ride-hailing fastest in Texas. The sources disagree on the numbers, and a registry count does not show how many vehicles are actually carrying passengers.
open_questions: Which registry figures are correct, since the two sources report different Tesla totals?
How many registered Tesla and Waymo vehicles are actively carrying passengers?
Which city will receive the next batch of Cybercabs, according to the sources?

headline: Robotera deploys 45 M7 humanoids at China Post Hangzhou hub

facts.text: ROBOTERA announced on November 26, 2026 that 45 of its humanoid robots have been deployed for parcel induction at China Post's Hangzhou Postal District Center.
China Post's Hangzhou Postal District Center officially launched testing of ROBOTERA's robots in April 2026.
According to ROBOTERA, this is the largest-scale deployment of robots for testing in comparable postal operations nationwide.
The robots can independently pick parcels, reorient them, identify and reject irregularly shaped parcels, place them onto induction platforms, and handle operational exceptions.
According to ROBOTERA, induction efficiency rose from 500–600 parcels per hour in initial testing to about 1,200 parcels per hour during specific testing periods.
ROBOTERA reports operational accuracy has exceeded 90%.
A Gasgoo report says the system was deployed for testing in early September and later surpassed 1,500 items per hour.
The Gasgoo report says the 45 M7 robots were deployed in partnership with CONVEY (Shenzhen).
The Hangzhou branch plans to accelerate adoption of automated equipment, including intelligent sorting and security inspection systems, across more operations.
A separate Guangdong rollout covered 11 postal hubs in eight cities, according to ROBOTERA's earlier announcement reported by unite.ai.

entities: China Post Hangzhou Postal District Center
context: ROBOTERA is a Chinese robotics company that develops general-purpose humanoid robots. China Post is the national postal operator, and its Hangzhou center sorts parcels, where induction means placing parcels onto the platforms that feed sorting systems.
why_it_matters: The deployment is described as one of the largest robot pilots in postal operations in China, suggesting automation of parcel handling at scale. Postal operators and logistics firms watching humanoid robots are most directly affected.
open_questions: Whether the induction efficiency and accuracy gains can be sustained across the full facility rather than during specific test periods.
How far automation will extend into intelligent sorting and security inspection, which the branch has said it plans to pursue.

headline: Pentagon in preliminary talks with GM and Ford on drone component production

facts.text: The Pentagon confirmed preliminary talks with General Motors, Ford and major suppliers about producing drone components.
The talks are part of a push toward a new autonomous warfare command.
Washington is looking to Detroit's idle capacity and established supply chains for the work.
Auto executives are questioning whether thin margins make the drone work a sustainable business.
Combat technology expert Louis Libin said the auto industry can close important parts of the production gap but full surge capacity requires more.
Libin said GM's recent achievement was delivering missile housing components in 22 days, which shows the value of existing manufacturing expertise.
Libin warned that small drones need frequent upgrades, creating tension between military needs and manufacturers' need for stable demand.
Libin said deeper involvement by auto suppliers in unmanned systems would raise security and supply-chain questions because drones can function as connected sensors and computers.

context: General Motors and Ford are major US automakers that historically built vehicles and, during World War II, shifted factories to military production. Drone components such as motors, batteries, sensors and electronics are made by a wide network of suppliers, so a manufacturing push depends on those supply chains. The Pentagon's reported interest reflects efforts to scale up unmanned systems production.
why_it_matters: The talks could bring idle automotive factories and suppliers into military drone production, affecting automakers and their suppliers. Analysts quoted in the report say the business case depends on payment terms and stable contracts given frequent drone upgrades.
open_questions: Whether automakers will find drone component production a sustainable business given thin margins.
What contracts, payment terms and volumes the Pentagon would offer.
How the proposed autonomous warfare command would be structured and funded.

headline: Boston Dynamics expands GlobalFoundries partnership; Korea's IL eyed for Atlas supply chain

facts.text: Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries expanded their collaboration to deploy Spot quadruped robots across GF's global semiconductor fabs.
GlobalFoundries will be the first customer outside the automotive industry to begin testing Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot.
Spot deployments will expand to GF manufacturing sites in Malta, New York; Burlington, Vermont; Dresden, Germany; and Singapore.
Boston Dynamics said two Spot robots in Singapore completed more than 90,000 inspections in sub-fab areas since April, with a 99% mission success rate.
The two companies said they will begin testing Atlas on-site at GF facilities in early 2027.
GlobalFoundries' chief manufacturing officer Pradip Singh said Spot helped the company shift from reactive to predictive maintenance.
GL Research, an independent research firm, expects Korean company IL to join the component supply chain for Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot.
Media reports in October said Hyundai Mobis would lead supply of Atlas headlamps and vision-recognition components, with IL and others as partners.
Boston Dynamics is reportedly pursuing production of components for 10,000 Atlas units through South Korean parts suppliers by 2027.
IL's third-quarter consolidated revenue was 33.4 billion won, up 14% year-on-year, with operating profit of 2.1 billion won.

context: Boston Dynamics is a robotics company known for the Spot quadruped robot and the Atlas humanoid robot, and is a subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group. GlobalFoundries is a semiconductor chip manufacturer with fabrication plants around the world. Spot is used for routine inspection and monitoring of industrial facilities.
why_it_matters: The GlobalFoundries deal shows humanoid and quadruped robots moving into semiconductor manufacturing, a sector that depends on precise, reliable monitoring. For Korean suppliers like IL, a role in the Atlas supply chain could mean new revenue as humanoid robots move toward mass production.
open_questions: Whether IL will actually win an Atlas component order is not confirmed; the sources describe it as expected.
Atlas testing at GF facilities is planned to start in early 2027 and its results are not yet known.
Whether Hyundai Mobis's leading role in Atlas headlamp and vision components will be finalized is not stated.

headline: EU delays Tesla self-driving vote to December 15

facts.text: The EU postponed its meeting to vote on bloc-wide approval of Tesla Assisted Driving from Dec. 1 to Dec. 15.
The vote was initially expected to conclude in October, making this another delay in the process.
Tesla has secured national approval in 12 EU countries.
Broader EU approval requires support from at least 15 of the bloc's 27 member states, representing 65% of its population.
The Netherlands was the first EU country to independently approve the technology, granting approval on April 10.
Tesla replaced the Full Self-Driving (Supervised) name with Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe.
Tesla reduced the maximum speed offset from 50% to 10% above the posted limit, resetting to zero each time the vehicle starts.
If the EU rejects wider approval, existing national authorizations could be invalidated, leaving customers in the 12 approved countries unable to use the system.
Tesla shares slipped 1.18% to $380.14 at the November 25 close after the delay was announced.
No reason has been given for the delay, according to the source.
Elon Musk said on the third-quarter call that he would be surprised if approval took longer than the first quarter of 2027.
Germany is a particularly important market for Tesla, and its support would lift EU population coverage to about 47%, according to GuruFocus.

context: The EU approves vehicle technology on a bloc-wide basis through a committee of member state representatives, after individual countries can approve it nationally. Tesla's system was first approved by the Netherlands and then recognized by other countries one by one. Driver-assistance systems like this require the driver to stay attentive, unlike fully autonomous driving.
why_it_matters: Tesla's European expansion of its assisted-driving software depends on this vote, and its software revenue growth could be affected. Customers in the 12 countries that have already approved the system would be affected if the EU rejects wider approval.
open_questions: Whether the EU committee will approve Tesla Assisted Driving on December 15.
Whether Germany, a key large market, will support approval.
The reason for the delay, which has not been given.

headline: Waymo stumbles on freeways despite city success

facts.text: A driverless Waymo was filmed trying to pass two California Highway Patrol cruisers during a traffic break on Interstate 280 on November 6.
The California DMV last week banned Waymo vehicles from all state interstates after a series of freeway incidents.
Between October and November 2026, Waymo reported 11 cases in which its vehicles drove into freeway lanes closed for construction, according to a recently filed recall.
Waymo paused commercial freeway rides across all its U.S. markets last week.
Earlier this year Waymo temporarily halted freeway rides after its robotaxis entered active construction zones in Arizona and California, and issued a recall in June.
Waymo gradually resumed freeway operations in late July after updating its software.
Phil Koopman, a Carnegie Mellon University researcher, says Waymo is using recalls as Band-Aids and that the recall did not fix the freeway problem.
In response to the DMV order, Waymo said its vehicles had not crashed or injured anyone while driving through restricted freeway areas.
Waymo said its ridehailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week.
Waymo said in late 2025 it was ready to drive on freeways, and co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov said freeway driving is easy to learn but very hard to master without a human backup.

context: Waymo is an autonomous ridehailing company that operates driverless robotaxis, mainly on city streets. Freeways are high-speed roads, so driverless cars there must handle merging, lane closures and construction zones with little margin for error. A state DMV can suspend or restrict the permits that let driverless vehicles operate on public roads.
why_it_matters: The freeway pause and state ban limit Waymo's service, which customers say makes some trips longer because highways are avoided. Experts argue that repeated recalls without fixes raise safety concerns for riders and road users, especially at highway speeds.
open_questions: When Waymo will be allowed to resume freeway operations in California.
Whether the recalls fully address the construction-zone and perception problems.
What solution Waymo is working on with California regulators.

headline: IFR: Robot density in manufacturing reaches new peak

facts.text: The International Federation of Robotics (IFR) reported that global average robot density in manufacturing has reached a record high.
South Korea leads the world in robot density with 1,066 industrial robots per 10,000 employees.
Singapore ranks second with 873 robots per 10,000 employees, and Germany ranks third with 469.
IFR says the new global average baseline has risen to 152 robots per 10,000 employees.
Robot density in the European Union rose about 35% from 2020 to 2025, reaching a record 240 units.
North America's robot density rose about 24% from 2020 to 2025, reaching 214 units.
The United States ranks 8th worldwide with 323 robots per 10,000 employees.
Japan ranks 4th globally with 452 robots per 10,000 employees.
China, the world's largest market for industrial robots, has a robot density of 193 units per 10,000 employees, ranking 19th globally.
China's robot density increased 147% from 2020 through 2025, according to IFR.

context: Robot density is the number of operational industrial robots per 10,000 employees in a sector, usually manufacturing, which lets countries of different economic sizes be compared on a common basis. The International Federation of Robotics is an industry organization that publishes annual statistics on industrial robots. Its previous robot density report was also led by South Korea, Singapore and Germany.
why_it_matters: Higher robot density signals greater automation in factories, which affects manufacturers and workers competing across regions. The report shows automation rising fastest in Asia and China over 2020-2025, while the EU and North America also grew.

headline: Lute Robotics raises $20 million for touch-based physical AI

facts.text: Lute Robotics has raised $20 million in combined pre-seed and seed funding to build a physical AI platform.
The seed round was co-led by OTB Ventures and Forward.one, after a pre-seed round co-led by Credo Ventures and Seedcamp.
Other investors include Inovo VC, Borusan Ventures, ff Venture Capital and angel investor Naval Ravikant.
Lute is developing foundation models that let robots use tactile information alongside visual data.
Lute co-designed compact, elastomer-based tactile sensors and built a portable system to collect tactile data for training.
Lute introduced Lute-0, its first video-action model, which translates how scenes change over time into robotic movements.
Lute says Lute-0 was pre-trained with substantially less data and a quarter of the training steps of π0.5, a leading open-source robot foundation model.
In internal evaluations across five retail manipulation tasks, Lute says Lute-0 beat π0.5 on success rates and showed about twofold lower latency.
Lute says its technology is operating at Europe's largest automotive parts distributor and in hospital corridors, about ten months after its founding.
Lute's software monitors tasks, pauses when something goes wrong, and hands control to a remote human operator.

context: Lute is a physical AI startup, meaning it builds AI software that controls robots acting in the real world. Foundation models are large AI models trained on broad data that can be adapted to many robot tasks. Tactile sensing means a robot feeling contact, such as grip force and slippage, rather than relying only on cameras.
why_it_matters: Lute says giving robots a sense of touch addresses a limitation of vision-only systems, which may help robots handle fragile or slippery objects in retail, warehousing and logistics. System integrators without in-house AI teams could deploy such robots with Lute's help, according to OTB Ventures' investment director.
open_questions: How the company's claimed performance results will hold up outside its internal evaluations.
Which partners and hardware platforms Lute will expand to with the new funding.
The names of the automotive parts distributor and retailers it works with are not given in the sources.

headline: Eric Trump-backed robot startup's employees lose health insurance as it seeks $150 million lifeline

facts.text: Employees of Foundation Future Industries, a humanoid robotics startup backed by Eric Trump, have lost employer-provided health benefits after weeks without pay.
Foundation told employees that benefits administered by Rippling ended retroactively to October, according to an internal memo reported by CNBC.
A human resources manager wrote that because the last pay run through Rippling was in October, the benefits had been ended with them retroactively.
Foundation promised to reimburse workers for COBRA continuation coverage and find a replacement provider.
Rippling disputed Foundation's account, saying clients who fail to meet payroll and benefits obligations over multiple months receive a warning before termination.
Employees last received paychecks on October 15, and some worry about a missed payday on November 30.
CNBC first reported the unpaid wages on November 14, alongside a $4.6 million company loan that co-founder and CEO Sankaet Pathak took in 2025.
Pathak told employees the loan arrangement had no relationship to the current cash situation, according to a Reuters report.
Foundation is pursuing a bridge loan ahead of a possible $150 million investment from South Korea's Base Group.
Reuters reported on November 19 that Base confirmed it was considering funding, but no deal was final.

context: Foundation Future Industries is a humanoid robotics startup. COBRA is a federal rule that generally lets workers who lose employer coverage keep it temporarily, though they usually must pay the full premium themselves. Rippling is a payroll and benefits administration service that companies use to run pay and benefits.
why_it_matters: Employees who have gone weeks without pay have also lost employer health coverage, which leaves some worried about affording rent and family medical care. The dispute over who is responsible and the uncertain investment affect the company's workers and its ability to keep operating.
open_questions: Whether Base Group will finalize its possible $150 million investment.
Whether Foundation can afford to reimburse COBRA coverage and find a replacement benefits provider.
Whether employees will be paid on November 30.

headline: Humyn Labs raises $47M Series A for physical AI

facts.text: Humyn Labs announced a $47 million Series A funding round.
The $47 million comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel.
The round also includes a $21 million venture debt round led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.
Humyn Labs was founded in 2026 by serial entrepreneurs Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta.
According to the company, Humyn Labs captures real-world work across factories, warehouses, farms and homes to train robots.
The company says it has surpassed $50 million in annualized revenue within six months of operations.
The company says it runs capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.
Agarwal said the funding will help strengthen research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand globally.
Accel partner Pratik Agarwal said Humyn Labs has the technical depth, customer pull, and ambition to be a category leader.

context: Physical AI refers to artificial intelligence that controls robots or machines interacting with the physical world. Training such systems requires large amounts of real-world data showing how humans perform tasks. A Series A is an early-stage venture funding round, typically following seed funding.
why_it_matters: The funding signals investor interest in data infrastructure for physical AI, which Humyn Labs says will serve frontier AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers. Factories, warehouses and farms that supply work data to such systems could also be affected.
open_questions: How the funds will be deployed beyond the three areas the company listed in the article.
Whether the company's stated revenue and growth targets will be achieved.

headline: XPeng to trial IRON humanoid as store assistant in its retail stores in Q1 2027

facts.text: XPeng said at its Nov. 25 AI Day in Guangzhou that its IRON humanoid is scheduled to start training as a store assistant in Q1 2027.
XPeng is targeting a public release of IRON in the second quarter of 2027.
XPeng says IRON would train in its retail outlets from January to March 2027, with public release planned between April and June.
XPeng unveiled the Turing Physical AI Architecture, also called VLA 3.0, designed to give its cars and robots a common technological foundation.
The Nov. 25 announcement did not specify how many stores or robots would participate, nor report results from store training.
XPeng president Brian Gu previously envisioned a robot that could greet buyers, explain features, and walk customers around a vehicle.
XPeng's chairman and CEO He Xiaopeng appeared on stage alongside the IRON robot at the AI Day event.
XPeng said it has commenced driverless passenger trials and aims to launch demonstration operations in selected locations before the end of 2026.

context: XPeng is a Chinese electric vehicle maker. A humanoid robot is a human-shaped machine designed to perform tasks like greeting people and explaining products. A store assistant role would have the robot help showroom visitors with routine questions before handing off to human staff.
why_it_matters: If the trial works, car dealership customers and staff could see robots handling routine showroom questions. Retailers considering such robots would need evidence on accuracy and time savings, which XPeng has not yet published.
open_questions: How many stores and robots will take part in the trial?
Will results from store training be published, and how well will IRON perform?
What will a robot cost to run for a retailer?

headline: OpenAI model tops humanoid simulation benchmark from Artificial Analysis, ahead of Google and Anthropic

facts.text: Artificial Analysis released the AA-Robotics-Sim v0.1 humanoid benchmark on November 25.
OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra outperformed rival models from Anthropic and Google in the benchmark.
The benchmark tested nine language models controlling a simulated Unitree G1 humanoid robot.
Astra finished 13.5 points ahead of its closest competitor on a 100-point scale.
Not a single piece of laundry made it inside the washing machine during the evaluation.
Across 90 dishwasher trials, the models placed only five dishes in the rack.
Researchers identified grasping as a persistent problem for the models.
All nine models earned full marks in warehouse navigation without moving packages.
In a separate experiment with a breakable dish, seven models broke it at least once, including Astra.
OpenAI claimed two of the top three spots across the 10 household and industrial assignments.

context: Artificial Analysis is an independent organization that benchmarks AI models. The Unitree G1 is a humanoid robot made by Unitree Robotics, a Chinese company. In this test, language models write code that directs the simulated robot's movements, while a separate controller keeps it balanced.
why_it_matters: The results suggest that current frontier language models can direct a humanoid robot through some tasks such as navigation but remain unreliable at grasping and manipulation-heavy chores like laundry and dishwashing. Consumers considering home humanoid robots, and companies deploying them, are affected by this gap.
open_questions: Whether the simulated results would hold on physical robots is not addressed by the benchmark alone.
Whether models can improve at grasping, which researchers identified as a persistent problem, is not yet known.

headline: Figure AI answers Musk's 'staged demo' criticism with apple-picking video

facts.text: Figure AI released a video on November 23 showing its Figure 03 humanoid robot picking up an apple, with the table moved, and picking it up again.
Brett Adcock, Figure AI's founder and CEO, posted the video on X saying the robot was never trained in this environment and moved fully autonomously.
Musk made the criticism at the Tomorrow X Summit on November 18, saying most humanoid robot demonstrations are staged or rely on pre-programming.
Musk illustrated his point with an apple on a table, arguing that moving the table would throw off a robot instructed to pick up the apple.
Adcock wrote that the video shows Figure running Helix, zero shot and fully autonomous.
Musk said Tesla's Optimus development is progressing and that an authentic demonstration could come within a month or two.
Some online users praised Figure's progress, while others questioned how many attempts the video took and whether the robot truly operated autonomously.
Some analysts say it is unclear whether Adcock reproduced the scenario Musk had in mind, since Musk did not specify whether the robot was already moving when the table was moved.
Figure AI says its robots have run 420 home trials across 30 homes, completing 237 of them (about 56%).

context: Figure AI is a U.S. humanoid robot startup, and Figure 03 is its current humanoid robot model. Tesla CEO Elon Musk is developing his own humanoid robot, Optimus. Humanoid robot demonstrations are often criticized as staged, meaning a robot's movements may be pre-programmed or recorded rather than produced by real-time perception and decision-making.
why_it_matters: The dispute centers on whether humanoid robots can perform tasks autonomously in changing conditions, which matters to investors, buyers and observers judging claims from Figure AI and Tesla. Musk's test sets a standard that also applies to Tesla's own pending Optimus demonstration.
open_questions: How many takes were needed to produce the Figure AI video, which the sources do not report.
Whether the robot was already in motion when the table was moved, as Musk did not specify.
Whether Tesla will release an Optimus demonstration meeting Musk's standard within the stated timeframe.

headline: VW ID. Buzz robotaxi hits LA streets; VW's $18,000 self-driving sedan shows China's lead
Auterion and partners to build drone manufacturing facility in Germany

facts.text: Auterion and partners plan a joint venture to build a drone manufacturing facility in Germany.
The joint venture is backed by German government funding, according to a Reuters report cited by the source.
The venture will initially produce the Shrike FPV drone, which keeps a continuous line-of-sight link between operator and aircraft.
At a later stage, the venture will produce Skyfall interceptors, combining Skyfall airframes with Auterion avionics.
The total investment is estimated at hundreds of millions of euros.
The drones are intended for both the German and Ukrainian armed forces.
Auterion CEO Lorenz Meier told Breaking Defense that Auterion and Skyfall have delivered guidance systems and real-time target detection systems to Ukrainian units.
The partner companies describe the joint venture as part of broad, ongoing cooperation with Ukraine.
Auterion operates from both the United States and Munich, Germany.

context: Auterion is a company that develops autonomous software and avionics for drones, and it has supplied such systems to Ukraine. FPV drones are first-person-view drones flown by an operator who sees the camera feed live. Interceptor drones are designed to intercept and destroy other drones or aerial threats.
why_it_matters: The plant would give the German military a domestic source of the drone types Ukrainian forces rely on weekly, reducing dependence on foreign supply. It also signals growing industrial drone production in Europe.
open_questions: The source does not give the facility's location, capacity or completion date.
The source does not state the exact funding amount or how it is split between the partners.

headline: Tesla FSD v15 removes interventions menu, adds pothole and animal detection

facts.text: Tesla's FSD v15 update removed the Interventions menu that had been introduced with v14.
The Interventions menu offered four options: Parking, Navigation, Critical, and Other.
The menu would not disappear until the user selected one of the options.
Many owners selected Critical every time to dismiss the menu, though that option is usually meant for serious incidents.
Tesla is expected to reduce the number of critical interventions by 25 times with FSD v15.
The v15 update adds avoidance of potholes and debris on the road, navigation improvements, and a new Reality View feature.
The v15 rollout began for Early Access Program participants on a weekend before November 26, 2026.
Tesla has not said why it removed the Interventions menu; the source suggests it may have been due to owner complaints or that the company no longer found it useful.

context: Full Self-Driving (FSD) is Tesla's driver-assistance software, which requires the driver to stay attentive and take over control when needed. Early Access Program participants test new versions before wider release. An intervention is any moment a driver takes control from the system.
why_it_matters: Owners who use FSD will no longer have to pick a reason each time they take over control, which removes a step that many found frustrating. Tesla's projected 25-fold cut in critical interventions, if borne out, would affect the many drivers relying on the system.
open_questions: Has the projected 25 times reduction in critical interventions been independently verified?
What exactly prompted Tesla to remove the Interventions menu?
How will Tesla identify the reasons for interventions now that the menu is gone?
